pages.title: VunaPOS
pages.html:
VunaPOS is the retail and restaurant point-of-sale workspace for ERPNext.

It provides a fast and focused selling experience while relying on ERPNext for the business-critical parts of the workflow, including items, customers, warehouses, stock, taxes, payment methods, invoices, and accounting.

It acts as a point-of-sale orchestration layer that sits between:

  • Items, what is being sold
  • Customers, who is making the purchase
  • Stock, where the items are coming from
  • Payments, how the sale is settled
  • Invoices, the final accounting transaction
  • Printing, how the customer receives proof of purchase

VunaPOS handles everything from item search and cart management to customer selection, payment processing, invoice creation, batch and serial number allocation, and receipt printing.

It is ideal for retail stores, supermarkets, restaurants, pharmacies, wholesalers, and other businesses that require a fast and reliable point-of-sale experience connected directly to ERPNext.

Why VunaPOS

Many point-of-sale systems become difficult to use when faced with real business requirements such as:

  • Inclusive and exclusive taxes
  • Multiple payment methods
  • Batch-controlled and serialised items
  • Held sales and interrupted checkouts
  • Real-time stock validation
  • Customer-specific pricing
  • External payment gateways
  • Sales Invoice and POS Invoice workflows

VunaPOS addresses these challenges by:

  • Using ERPNext as the source of truth for stock, taxes, pricing, customers, payments, and accounting.
  • Providing a clean and focused cashier interface without duplicating ERPNext business logic.
  • Supporting both Sales Invoice and POS Invoice workflows based on the configured POS Settings.
  • Keeping critical calculations and validations on the backend, reducing inconsistencies between the user interface and ERPNext.

The result is a POS system that is practical, extensible, and suitable for real-world ERPNext deployments.

Key Features

  • Fast Item Search: Find items using their name, item code, or barcode.
  • Customer Selection: Search and select existing customers or use the default customer configured in the POS Profile.
  • Cart Management: Add items, change quantities, remove items, clear the cart, and review invoice totals before checkout.
  • Hold and Restore: Save an active sale as a draft invoice and restore it later without losing the transaction.
  • Flexible Invoicing: Create either a Sales Invoice or POS Invoice depending on the configured ERPNext POS Settings.
  • Tax Handling: Support inclusive and exclusive taxes using ERPNext tax calculation rules.
  • Batch Allocation: Automatically allocate stock from valid batches, including quantities distributed across multiple batches.
  • Serial Number Allocation: Automatically allocate available serial numbers for serialised items during checkout.
  • Multiple Payment Modes: Use the payment methods configured in the ERPNext POS Profile.
  • Payment Gateway Support: Process and verify payments through supported gateways such as M-Pesa STK Push and C2B transactions.
  • Checkout Validation: Validate stock, taxes, payment totals, batch allocation, serial numbers, and invoice status before submission.
  • Receipt Printing: Render and print receipts using ERPNext Print Formats.

Choose your starting point

  • New counter? Follow Setting Up, then Open and Close Your Shift.
  • Making a retail sale? Start with Complete a Sale.
  • Taking an order for later delivery? Use Sales Orders.
  • Running a restaurant? Start with Restaurant Overview.

Restaurant mode adds table-based visits, repeat ordering rounds, menu sections, kitchen tickets and a kitchen display. Waiters place orders, chefs prepare them, and authorised cashiers bill the visit. The selling screen, customers, payment methods and receipt printing remain familiar.

Know what is saved

A completed invoice, saved draft or placed restaurant order is different from an unsaved cart. Save a draft before leaving an unfinished retail sale. Do not assume refreshing the browser preserves your cart or that a cached catalogue allows offline checkout.

The configured invoice type remains Sales Invoice or POS Invoice. A Sales Order records an order to fulfil, not an immediate stock issue. Restaurant prepared orders additionally check ingredients and reserve preparation stock.

See Connection and Submission Recovery if a payment or checkout is interrupted.

pages.title: Installation
pages.html:
This page is for the administrator or hosting provider installing VunaPOS. Cashiers should start with Open and Close Your Shift.

Before installing

Use a working ERPNext site with the Frappe and ERPNext version supported by your chosen VunaPOS branch. This guide reflects the application tested with version 16; it is not a promise of compatibility with every later version. Back up an existing site before installing or upgrading.

VunaPOS requires ERPNext. A payments connector is optional unless you need integrated STK/C2B payments.

Managed hosting

Ask your hosting provider to add VunaPOS to the ERPNext site. The Frappe Cloud marketplace is one installation option. Confirm that the selected app branch matches the site's ERPNext version.

Install in an existing bench

From the bench directory, obtain the app with:

bench get-app https://github.com/navariltd/vunapos

If this is a new site, create it and install ERPNext before VunaPOS:

bench new-site vunapos.localhost
bench --site vunapos.localhost install-app erpnext

Install VunaPOS, migrate and build its assets:

bench --site vunapos.localhost install-app vunapos
bench --site vunapos.localhost migrate
bench build --app vunapos

Use your own site name in place of the example. Start the bench normally for development, then open /vunapos on that site. In production, use the hosting provider's normal deployment process rather than running a development server.

After installation or an upgrade

  1. Follow Setting Up. Installing the app alone does not create your operational items, accounts or cashier profiles.
  2. Confirm assigned users can open the selling terminal from VunaPOS or /vunapos.
    Administrators can use the separate VunaPOS Setup icon to open POS Profiles
    and the Desk setup sidebar. On an existing site, reload Desk after deployment
    if its desktop still shows the previous app entries.
  3. Test a sale using the actual warehouse, price list, taxes and payment accounts.
  4. After an upgrade, refresh terminals only after saving unfinished work. Review any pending submissions before selling the same cart again.

For restaurant operation, continue with Set Up a Restaurant. Do not use demonstration recipes, stock receipts or shared demo credentials on a production site.

pages.title: Setting Up

headings.title: Open setup or the selling terminal
Enable only the workflows this counter needs

pages.html:
Once you have installed the app, you should first configure VunaPOS using the standard ERPNext POS Settings and POS Profile documents.

These documents define how invoices are created, which users can access the POS, which company and warehouse are used, how payments are recorded, and which defaults apply during checkout.

Before opening VunaPOS for the first time, it is recommended to complete the basic ERPNext selling and accounting setup and then review these two documents.

Open setup or the selling terminal

Use VunaPOS Setup on the desktop to open POS Profiles with the VunaPOS Desk
sidebar. This is where you configure counters and access the setup records your
role permits. Restaurant navigation is also available in its own Desk sidebar.

Use VunaPOS to open the selling terminal. Keeping these separate lets cashiers
start selling without first navigating through configuration pages. A setup link
does not grant permission to change records; normal ERPNext permissions still apply.

Recommended Setup Flow

  1. Configure Company and Accounts
  2. Create Warehouses
  3. Configure Items and Item Prices
  4. Set up Modes of Payment
  5. Configure POS Settings
  6. Create a POS Profile
  7. Assign POS Users
  8. Open VunaPOS and complete a test sale

Following this order helps ensure that stock, pricing, payments, taxes, and invoice creation behave predictably.

POS Settings

The POS Settings document controls the general invoice behavior used by VunaPOS.

One of the most important settings is the invoice type that should be created when a sale is completed.

VunaPOS supports:

  • Sales Invoice
  • POS Invoice

The selected option determines which ERPNext document VunaPOS creates and submits during checkout.

Invoice Type

Field Description Usage
Invoice Type Determines whether VunaPOS creates a Sales Invoice or POS Invoice. Select the document type that matches your accounting and operational requirements.

Sales Invoice

When Sales Invoice is selected, VunaPOS creates a standard ERPNext Sales Invoice.

This option is suitable when:

  • You want to use the standard Sales Invoice workflow
  • You want realtime stock and accounting transaction ledgers
  • You need receivables and customer outstanding balances
  • You want to support credit sales
  • Your accounting process already relies heavily on Sales Invoice

The invoice can still behave like a POS transaction when the required POS fields and payment rows are provided.

POS Invoice

When POS Invoice is selected, VunaPOS creates an ERPNext POS Invoice.

This option is suitable when:

  • You want a transaction document specifically designed for point-of-sale activity
  • Most transactions are paid immediately
  • You want to keep retail transactions separate from regular Sales Invoices
  • You are using ERPNext’s POS Invoice workflow and related reports

Note: VunaPOS uses the option selected in POS Settings automatically. The cashier does not choose the invoice type during each sale.

POS Profile

The POS Profile document acts as the main configuration center for a VunaPOS counter.

It defines the company, warehouse, customer defaults, payment methods, pricing, print settings, and user assignments used when a cashier opens VunaPOS.

A POS Profile answers questions such as:

  • Which company is making the sale?
  • Which warehouse should stock be deducted from?
  • Which customer should be used by default?
  • Which price list should be applied?
  • Which payment methods are available?
  • Which users can access this POS setup?
  • Which print format should be used?
  • Which accounts should receive payments?

To open POS Profile, go to:

Home > Selling > POS > POS Profile

Company and Warehouse

These fields determine the accounting company and stock location used by the POS.

Field Description Usage
Company The ERPNext company used for invoice creation and accounting entries. Select the company that owns the POS operation.
Warehouse The warehouse from which stock is issued when items are sold. Select the warehouse used by the branch, store, or counter.
Currency The currency used for selling and payment amounts. Usually inherited from the company or price list.

The selected warehouse is also used when VunaPOS checks stock availability, batch quantities, and serial number availability.

Warning: If the warehouse is incorrect, stock may be deducted from the wrong location.

Customer Defaults

The POS Profile can define a default customer for transactions.

Field Description Usage
Customer The customer automatically selected when VunaPOS opens. Commonly set to a Walk-in Customer for retail sales.
Customer Group (on Customer) Maintained on the selected Customer, not a separate profile default. Helps determine customer pricing and reporting.
Territory (on Customer) Maintained on the Customer record. Used for customer setup and sales reporting.

The cashier can select another customer. Confirm the customer before taking payment, because customer selection can change prices, loyalty information and available shipping addresses.

A common setup is:

Customer: Walk-in Customer
Customer Group: All Customer Groups
Territory: All Territories

Price List and Pricing

The profile must have an enabled Selling price list in its currency; a Buying-only list cannot be used to sell. Customer defaults may choose another list. If permitted, the cashier's explicit price-list selection applies to that transaction. See Prices and Discounts.

Field Description Usage
Selling Price List The ERPNext price list used when loading item prices. Select the price list used by the store or branch.
Currency Currency associated with the price list. Controls item and invoice currency.
Ignore Pricing Rule Determines whether ERPNext pricing rules should be ignored. Leave disabled if you want standard pricing rules to apply.

VunaPOS relies on ERPNext pricing rules and item prices rather than maintaining a separate pricing system.

Modes of Payment

Modes of Payment define how customers can settle a sale.

Examples include:

  • Cash
  • M-Pesa
  • Card
  • Bank
  • Mobile Money
Field Description Usage
Mode of Payment The payment method available during checkout. Add every payment method that cashiers should be able to select.
Default Marks the payment method that should be selected automatically. Useful when Cash is the most common payment method.
Account The ledger account used for the payment method. Required for correct accounting entries.

The payment rows configured in POS Profile are displayed on the VunaPOS checkout page.

For example:

Cash
M-Pesa
Card
Bank

Note: Each Mode of Payment should have the correct company account configured in ERPNext.

User Allocation

The POS Profile can be assigned to specific users.

Field Description Usage
Applicable For Users Defines which users are allowed to use the profile. Add each cashier or POS operator who should access VunaPOS.
User The ERPNext user account assigned to the profile. Select the correct cashier login.

When a cashier opens VunaPOS, the system resolves the POS Profile available to that user.

This allows different branches or counters to have separate:

  • Warehouses
  • Companies
  • Price lists
  • Payment methods
  • Customers
  • Print formats

Print Format

The print format determines how receipts or invoices are rendered after checkout.

Field Description Usage
Print Format The ERPNext Print Format used after invoice submission. Select a thermal receipt or standard invoice format.
Letter Head Optional company letterhead used in printing. Useful for A4 invoices or branded receipts.

For thermal printers, create or select a compact print format designed for narrow receipt paper.

Select a Print Format that actually exists on your site and matches the selected
invoice type. Ask the administrator to test its paper width and letterhead rather
than assuming a particular custom receipt format is installed.

Taxes and Charges

The POS Profile may define a default Sales Taxes and Charges Template.

Field Description Usage
Taxes and Charges The default tax template applied to the invoice. Use this for VAT, sales tax, or other standard charges.
Tax Category Used to apply tax rules based on the customer or transaction. Configure where tax categories are part of your setup.

VunaPOS uses ERPNext tax calculation as the source of truth.

It supports:

  • Inclusive taxes
  • Exclusive taxes
  • Item Tax Templates
  • Sales Taxes and Charges Templates
  • Backend-calculated totals

Accounting Defaults

The POS Profile also provides accounting values required during invoice submission.

These may include:

Field Description
Income Account The account credited when items are sold.
Expense Account The account used for cost or expense recognition.
Cost Center The cost center assigned to the transaction.
Write-Off Account Account used for approved write-off amounts.
Account for Change Amount Account used where cash tendered exceeds the sale amount.

Most of these values can be inherited from the Item, Company, Warehouse, or Mode of Payment configuration.

Example POS Profile

A simple retail configuration may look like:

POS Profile: Main Store POS
Company: Vuna Retail Ltd
Warehouse: Main Store - VR
Customer: Walk-in Customer
Selling Price List: Standard Selling
Currency: KES
Print Format: Thermal Receipt
Applicable User: cashier@example.com

Modes of Payment:

Cash
M-Pesa
Card

Taxes and Charges:

Kenya VAT 16%

Before Opening VunaPOS

Before launching VunaPOS, confirm that:

  • The correct invoice type is selected in POS Settings
  • The POS Profile is enabled
  • The cashier is assigned to the POS Profile
  • The company and warehouse are correct
  • A default customer is configured
  • A selling price list is selected
  • Modes of Payment have valid accounts
  • A print format is selected
  • Items have selling prices
  • Stock is available in the selected warehouse for invoice sales that issue stock

Media

POS Settings

Enable only the workflows this counter needs

Review the VunaPOS options on the POS Profile:

  • Default Order Type and Allow Order Type Change control whether staff start with invoices or can create Sales Orders.
  • Allow Credit Sales permits an invoice to retain a customer balance. Credit is a sale type, not a payment method named “Credit.”
  • Allow Sales Order Advance Payments permits order deposits; it does not turn an order into a stock issue.
  • Allow Customer Creation, Allow Customer Management, Allow Customer Payments, Allow Payment History and Allow Payment Reconciliation control the related pages/actions. Users still need ERPNext permissions.
  • Allow Service Items includes non-stock sales items when needed.
  • Allow Returns controls access to invoice returns from this counter.
  • Allow Price List Switching and Allowed Price Lists define permitted transaction-level choices.
  • Allow Delivery Charges requires a non-stock Delivery Charge Item. Allow Delivery Charge Change controls amount entry.
  • New Cart Item Position places new lines at the top or bottom of the cart.

Use Checkout Fields and Approval Workflows for extra checkout information, Staff Access and PIN Controls for approval settings, and Connection and Submission Recovery for background submission.

For restaurants, set POS Mode to Restaurant and follow the separate restaurant setup sequence. Do not try to configure tables by changing the warehouse or Item Group filters alone.

Next Steps

After completing the configuration:

  1. Open VunaPOS.
  2. Confirm the correct POS Profile is loaded.
  3. Search for an item.
  4. Add the item to the cart.
  5. Select or confirm the customer.
  6. Complete a test checkout.
  7. Verify the created invoice and accounting entries.
  8. Print the receipt.

Related Topics

  • Complete a Sale
  • Find Items and Choose Units
  • Customers and Shipping Addresses
  • Cash, Split Payments and Credit Sales
  • Print Receipts

pages.title: Open and Close Your Shift
pages.html:
Use your own shift to record the sales and payments you handle. Sharing a POS Profile does not mean sharing an opening session.

Open your shift

  1. Sign in and open VunaPOS.
  2. Choose the correct POS Profile in the opening dialog. Your default profile is prioritised and marked in the selector; an existing shift may determine the active profile.
  3. Enter opening balances for the displayed payment methods. Declare the actual cash float, not the sales you expect to make.
  4. Select Start POS Session.

The default payment method appears first, followed by the others alphabetically. More rows scroll inside the dialog. If opening fails, read the error and correct the problem; do not open a different counter just to get past it.

One user cannot open another POS shift while they already have an open one. If you need another profile, close the current shift first.

During the shift

Check the profile and warehouse before selling. The profile determines available prices, stock, payment modes and permissions. In restaurants, both waiters and cashiers open their own shifts; kitchen-only users do not.

Use Profile for user information and theme preferences. On mobile the profile shortcut is in the header. The catalogue view icon changes between list and grid; the scan button opens the camera scanner.

Close and reconcile

  1. Finish or save unfinished work.
  2. Resolve pending invoice submissions before closing.
  3. Open Close Shift.
  4. Review the expected amounts for each payment method, opening amounts, sales, receipts and any displayed differences.
  5. Enter the amounts actually counted/received for each method and review differences with your supervisor.
  6. Complete the closing action.

An unresolved queued invoice can block closing. Follow Connection and Submission Recovery rather than recreating it. A restaurant waiter closes their own shift; the cashier's closing contains the payments collected by that cashier.

[Screenshot: Opening session dialog with a default profile, opening cash float and multiple payment methods]

[Screenshot: Close Shift showing expected, counted and difference amounts by payment method]

pages.title: Complete a Sale
pages.html:
Use this workflow when goods are being sold now. For an order to fulfil later, use Sales Orders. Restaurant staff should use Take Dine-in and Takeaway Orders.

Before you start

Sign in with your own user, open your POS shift and confirm the counter/profile. Prices, warehouse stock and payment methods depend on that profile. You need a connection to the server to finish checkout.

Make the sale

  1. Confirm the customer above the cart, or choose the correct customer. A named customer may have different prices or loyalty points.
  2. Select a shipping address below the customer when needed. Only addresses you may access are offered.
  3. Search for an item by name, code or barcode, or use the scanner. Choose a variant if the item has options.
  4. Review quantity and selling UOM on the cart line. Expand the line to change UOM, add a note or review batch/serial allocation.
  5. Check the selected price list, discounts you are allowed to enter, subtotal, taxes and grand total.
  6. Select Checkout. Enter any required checkout fields, delivery amount or walk-in Tax ID.
  7. Allocate the payable amount to the configured payment methods. If using an integrated gateway, wait for payment verification.
  8. Review the final total and select the completion action shown. Do not treat an opened checkout dialog as a completed sale.
  9. Confirm the result and invoice number. Print the receipt if needed.

An enabled approval workflow may save the transaction for approval instead of submitting it. Follow the available workflow action explicitly; see Checkout Fields and Approval Workflows.

If you need to pause

Use Hold to save an unfinished invoice. Find it under Sales History → Draft Invoices. Clearing the cart or refreshing an unsaved page is not the same as holding it.

On small screens the checkout footer shows Hold and Complete; some desktop actions are not shown there.

If checkout does not finish

Read the message before trying again. Correct stock/allocation problems or check a pending payment. If the result is unclear, check Sales History or the submission panel before starting another sale. Never collect a second payment merely because the first response was delayed.

[Screenshot: Completed retail checkout showing invoice number, payment result and receipt action]

pages.title: Find Items and Choose Units
pages.html:
Use the catalogue to choose what the customer is buying and the cart to confirm how much is being sold.

Find the right item

Search by item name, code or barcode. Use list or grid view and select an item to add it. A variant template opens a selection dialog: choose the actual size, style or other variant before adding it. Product bundles may require reviewing their component choices.

For administrators: enable the Item for selling, give it an Item Price in the relevant selling list and configure its UOM conversions. Non-stock items require Allow Service Items on the profile. Profile item filters and restaurant menus may further restrict availability.

Choose the selling unit

The Item's Sales UOM is the normal starting unit; otherwise the stock UOM is used. Expand a cart line and use Selling UOM to change it. Review the rate and quantity afterward; a carton and a piece need not have the same price.

Different UOMs of the same item can be separate cart lines. Use the action beside Selling UOM to add that item in another UOM. A new line follows the profile's top/bottom item-position setting. Selecting a UOM already present may merge into the matching line.

Read stock correctly

The visible balance uses the catalogue's selling unit. The information icon shows the stock-unit balance and conversion details.

Example: one carton contains 24 pieces. Two cartons and three pieces require 51 pieces in total. VunaPOS checks the combined requirement across rows of the same item; changing UOM does not create more stock.

For an invoice, if there is not enough stock for one normal sales unit but there is stock in the stock UOM, the POS can add the item in the stock UOM and show a notice. Check the notice, line unit and price. It does not silently reduce an existing order quantity.

Ordinary retail Sales Orders do not use this invoice-stock fallback. Prepared restaurant items use ingredient/preparation checks instead.

Quantity rejected or reverted

Read the stock message below the line. Reduce quantity, choose a valid UOM or ask stock staff to verify the profile warehouse. Quantities in a UOM marked “Must be Whole Number” cannot be fractional.

For tracked stock, see Batch and Serial Number Allocation.

[Screenshot: One item in Carton and Pcs rows, with Selling UOM and the stock-balance information tooltip]

pages.title: Customers and Shipping Addresses

headings.title: Walk-in customer, Tax ID and credit

pages.html:
Choose the customer before confirming prices and payment. A customer can affect the price list, taxes, credit balance and loyalty points.

Select or create a customer

Open the customer selector above the cart and search by the details available. Select the intended customer rather than another customer with a similar name.

If Allow Customer Creation is enabled and your user has permission, use the creation option in the selector for a simple customer. Maintain detailed accounting, credit and contact setup in ERPNext.

Customers opens the directory when enabled. Open a customer to review the details, balances and transactions you are permitted to see. Payment history and receiving payments may be restricted separately.

Choose a shipping address

  1. Select the customer.
  2. Use the shipping-address selector below the customer and above the cart.
  3. Review the formatted address shown, not just the address title.
  4. Choose another available address if this transaction is for a different location.

The primary address is preferred when available. Changing customer clears/reloads the address choices so an address from the previous customer is not carried into the new sale.

The selected address is saved with the supported invoice/order transaction. An address must be linked to that customer and accessible to you. If a customer has four addresses but permissions allow you only one, the selector does not grant access to the other three.

Create/share missing addresses through the authorised ERPNext address workflow; this selector does not create an address or bypass permissions.

Walk-in customer, Tax ID and credit

Use the shared walk-in customer for anonymous counter sales. A one-off Tax ID can be captured on an invoice without changing that shared customer; see Cash Customer Tax ID.

Use a named customer when you need a reliable customer balance or repeat-customer history. Confirm the customer's identity before receiving an advance, applying an old credit or redeeming points.

Restaurant visits lock the customer after an order round is placed. Choose the correct customer before sending the first order.

[Screenshot: Customer selector and shipping address selector showing two permitted addresses and the formatted selected address]

pages.title: Prices and Discounts
pages.html:
Use the displayed price list and checkout totals to confirm what the customer will pay. Item Prices, Pricing Rules and taxes are maintained in ERPNext.

Starting prices and transaction overrides

The normal starting price list is resolved in this order:

  1. Customer default price list.
  2. Customer Group default price list.
  3. POS Profile selling price list.
  4. Selling Settings default selling price list.

If the profile permits price-list switching, an explicit selection on the cart takes precedence for that transaction. The choices must be enabled selling lists available to the user/profile and use the profile currency. The override does not permanently change the customer's default; the next new sale returns to the normal default.

Administrators can use Allowed Price Lists to narrow the permitted choices. A Buying-only list cannot be used for selling.

Rates, units and promotions

An Item Price can apply to a particular UOM. If the sold unit changes, review the recalculated price. A system-calculated UOM/pricing-rule change is different from a cashier typing a manual rate.

Pricing Rules may depend on customer, group, dates, quantity or other conditions. The catalogue is a preview; adding items and changing quantities can change the applicable offer. Review the calculated cart and checkout total rather than assuming every catalogue price is final.

Manual rates and discounts depend on profile permissions and ERPNext validations. If an override is rejected, ask an authorised manager to review the setup; do not try to disguise the discount as another UOM.

When an administrator changes prices

Save the Item Price/Pricing Rule in ERPNext. Connected terminals refresh catalogue information, but this is not a promise that every terminal changes at the same instant. If a price looks old, save unfinished work and check the active list, UOM and customer before reloading.

Restaurant placed rounds retain their recorded prices; changing today's menu price does not rewrite an order already placed.

See Inclusive and Exclusive Item Taxes for tax interpretation.

[Screenshot: Price-list selector, a pricing-rule-adjusted cart line and the final checkout total]

pages.title: Inclusive and Exclusive Item Taxes

headings.title: Grand Total Is Lower Than Expected
Tax Display Differs From the Submitted Invoice

pages.html:
VunaPOS supports both inclusive and exclusive item tax calculation when ERPNext Item Tax Templates are used.

ERPNext normally treats taxes from an Item Tax Template as exclusive, meaning the tax amount is calculated and added on top of the item’s basic rate.

VunaPOS adds the Item Prices Include Tax option to the POS Profile so each POS setup can control how those item taxes should be interpreted.

Requirements

Before using item-level taxes in VunaPOS:

  1. Create the required Item Tax Templates in ERPNext.
  2. Assign the appropriate Item Tax Template to each item.
  3. Add the relevant tax accounts and rates.
  4. Open the POS Profile used by VunaPOS.
  5. Decide whether the configured item prices already include tax.

Item Prices Include Tax

The Item Prices Include Tax checkbox is available on the POS Profile.

Its behavior is:

Item Prices Include Tax Tax Behaviour
Checked Item prices are treated as tax-inclusive. The tax amount is extracted from the item rate.
Unchecked Item prices are treated as tax-exclusive. The tax amount is calculated and added on top of the item rate.

This option applies when VunaPOS processes taxes defined through Item Tax Templates.

Inclusive Taxes

Enable Item Prices Include Tax when the selling price shown for an item already contains the tax amount.

For example:

Item Rate: KES 116.00
VAT Rate: 16%

Because the tax is inclusive:

Net Amount: KES 100.00
Tax Included: KES 16.00
Grand Total: KES 116.00

The customer pays the displayed item price. The tax is extracted from that amount instead of being added again.

Configure Inclusive Taxes

  1. Open POS Profile.
  2. Select the profile used by VunaPOS.
  3. Enable Item Prices Include Tax.
  4. Save the POS Profile.
  5. Confirm that the item has the correct Item Tax Template.
  6. Reload VunaPOS before processing another sale.

When the item is added to the cart, VunaPOS treats the item rate as the final tax-inclusive selling price.

Exclusive Taxes

Leave Item Prices Include Tax unchecked when the item rate does not already contain tax.

For example:

Item Rate: KES 100.00
VAT Rate: 16%

Because the tax is exclusive:

Net Amount: KES 100.00
Tax Added: KES 16.00
Grand Total: KES 116.00

The tax is calculated on top of the item’s basic rate.

Configure Exclusive Taxes

  1. Open POS Profile.
  2. Select the profile used by VunaPOS.
  3. Leave Item Prices Include Tax unchecked.
  4. Save the POS Profile.
  5. Confirm that the item has the correct Item Tax Template.
  6. Reload VunaPOS before processing another sale.

How VunaPOS Determines Tax Behaviour

When an item has an Item Tax Template, VunaPOS checks the Item Prices Include Tax value on the active POS Profile.

If the option is checked:

  • the item rate is treated as inclusive of tax
  • the tax amount is extracted from the rate
  • the grand total remains equal to the tax-inclusive item total

If the option is unchecked:

  • the item rate is treated as exclusive of tax
  • the tax amount is calculated on top of the rate
  • the grand total increases by the calculated tax amount

VunaPOS uses the active POS Profile consistently throughout the sale so that item display, cart totals, checkout totals, and the submitted invoice follow the same tax treatment.

Cart and Checkout Display

The cart and checkout page show the tax breakdown returned by the backend.

For inclusive taxes, the tax may appear as:

Subtotal: KES 100.00
VAT 16% · Included: KES 16.00
Grand Total: KES 116.00

For exclusive taxes, it may appear as:

Subtotal: KES 100.00
VAT 16% · Added: KES 16.00
Grand Total: KES 116.00

The frontend displays the calculated values but does not independently calculate the official tax total.

Mixed Items

An invoice may contain several items with different Item Tax Templates.

VunaPOS applies the tax rate associated with each item while using the POS Profile setting to determine whether the item prices are inclusive or exclusive.

For example:

Item A: VAT 16%
Item B: Zero-rated
Item C: VAT 8%

When Item Prices Include Tax is enabled, applicable taxes are extracted from the item prices.

When it is disabled, applicable taxes are added on top of the item rates.

Changing the Setting

Changing Item Prices Include Tax affects how VunaPOS interprets item prices for subsequent sales.

After changing the option:

  1. Save the POS Profile.
  2. Reload VunaPOS.
  3. Start a new sale.
  4. Add a taxed item.
  5. Review the cart totals before checkout.

Do not change the tax interpretation in the middle of an active sale.

Warning: The item prices and POS Profile tax setting must agree. Enabling inclusive tax for prices that exclude tax will understate the final amount. Leaving it disabled for prices that already include tax will add the tax twice.

Common Problems

Tax Is Being Added Twice

Cause

The item price already includes tax, but Item Prices Include Tax is not enabled.

Resolution

  1. Open the active POS Profile.
  2. Enable Item Prices Include Tax.
  3. Save the profile.
  4. Reload VunaPOS.
  5. Start a new sale and review the totals.

Grand Total Is Lower Than Expected

Cause

Item Prices Include Tax may be enabled even though the configured item rates exclude tax.

Resolution

  1. Confirm how the item prices were entered.
  2. Open the active POS Profile.
  3. Disable Item Prices Include Tax if the rates exclude tax.
  4. Reload VunaPOS and retry the sale.

Item Tax Is Not Applied

Cause

The item may not have an Item Tax Template, or the template may not contain the expected tax account and rate.

Resolution

  1. Open the Item in ERPNext.
  2. Confirm the Item Tax Template assignment.
  3. Review the tax account and rate.
  4. Add the item to a new VunaPOS sale.
  5. Confirm the tax appears in the cart.

Tax Display Differs From the Submitted Invoice

Cause

The active sale may have been created before the POS Profile or tax configuration changed.

Resolution

  1. Clear or hold the current sale.
  2. Reload VunaPOS.
  3. Start a new sale.
  4. Add the item again.
  5. Confirm that the cart and checkout totals match the submitted invoice.

Template taxes and service charges

This item-price setting does not replace the Sales Taxes and Charges Template. Review both the item tax assignment and the transaction's tax template. For a restaurant service-specific charge, see Build Menus and Item Choices.

pages.title: Cash Customer Tax ID

headings.title: When the Tax ID Field Appears
How VunaPOS Uses the Tax ID
Customer Tax ID Field Is Not Visible
Tax ID Is Not Included on the Invoice
Customer Should Not Be a Walk-in Customer

pages.html:
VunaPOS allows a cashier to enter a customer’s Tax ID when the selected customer is marked as a walk-in customer.

This is useful when a cash customer does not have a dedicated ERPNext Customer record but still requires an invoice containing their tax identification details, such as for eTIMS or business expense purposes.

The Tax ID is captured for the current sale and included on the invoice created by VunaPOS.

When the Tax ID Field Appears

The Customer Tax ID field is available when the selected customer is configured as a walk-in customer.

Is Walk-in Customer

If a regular customer is selected, VunaPOS uses the tax information already stored on that customer record.

This prevents the cashier from unnecessarily re-entering information that ERPNext already knows.

Enter a Customer Tax ID

To add a Tax ID for a walk-in customer:

  1. Open VunaPOS.
  2. Confirm that the selected customer is a walk-in customer.
  3. Add the required items to the cart.
  4. Open Checkout.
  5. Enter the customer’s Tax ID in the provided field.
  6. Review the invoice total and payment details.
  7. Complete the sale.

The Tax ID applies only to the current invoice unless the customer is later created as a permanent ERPNext Customer.

Example

A cash customer purchases goods worth KES 5,800.00 and requests an invoice for business use.

The cashier can use:

VunaPOS creates the invoice using the shared walk-in customer while attaching the entered Tax ID to that specific transaction.

This allows the customer to receive an invoice containing their tax information without creating a new Customer record for a one-time purchase.

How VunaPOS Uses the Tax ID

When the sale is completed, VunaPOS adds the entered Tax ID to the invoice created for the transaction.

The invoice may be either:

  • Sales Invoice
  • POS Invoice

The document type depends on the current POS Settings configuration.

The Tax ID is then available for downstream processes such as:

  • invoice printing
  • eTIMS integration
  • fiscal reporting
  • customer reference
  • transaction audit

VunaPOS does not replace the selected walk-in customer with a new Customer record.

Important Notes

Note: The Tax ID field is intended for walk-in customers who need their own tax details included on a single invoice.

Note: For regular customers, maintain the Tax ID on the ERPNext Customer record instead of entering it manually during every sale.

Warning: Confirm the Tax ID before completing checkout. An incorrect Tax ID may result in an incorrect fiscal or tax invoice.

Warning: Once the invoice is submitted, correcting the Tax ID may require cancelling or amending the transaction, depending on permissions and fiscal integration rules.

Tax ID and eTIMS

Where an eTIMS integration is installed, the entered Tax ID can be passed with the invoice information used for fiscalisation.

This allows a walk-in customer to receive a tax invoice containing their own identification details even though the transaction uses the shared walk-in Customer record.

The exact fiscal behaviour depends on the eTIMS application installed on the site.

VunaPOS itself captures the Tax ID and attaches it to the invoice. Any external fiscal submission is handled by the configured integration.

Common Problems

Customer Tax ID Field Is Not Visible

Cause

The selected customer may not be marked as a walk-in customer.

Resolution

  1. Confirm the selected customer.
  2. Open the Customer record in ERPNext.
  3. Verify that the customer is configured as a walk-in customer.
  4. Return to VunaPOS and select the customer again.

Tax ID Is Not Included on the Invoice

Cause

The Tax ID may not have been entered before checkout, or the invoice field used by the integration may not be configured correctly.

Resolution

  1. Confirm the Tax ID was entered before completing the sale.
  2. Open the submitted invoice.
  3. Check whether the Tax ID was saved.
  4. Review the installed eTIMS or fiscal integration configuration where applicable.

Tax ID Is Invalid

Cause

The value may be mistyped, or the installed fiscal integration may reject it. VunaPOS captures the entered Tax ID; it does not promise that it validates every country's tax-ID format.

Resolution

  1. Confirm the Tax ID with the customer.
  2. Correct the value before checkout.
  3. Retry the sale.

Customer Should Not Be a Walk-in Customer

Cause

The buyer may be a recurring customer whose details should be stored permanently.

Resolution

  1. Create or select the correct ERPNext Customer.
  2. Store the Tax ID on the Customer record.
  3. Use that customer for the sale instead of the shared walk-in customer.

pages.title: Batch and Serial Number Allocation

headings.title: Allocated Batch Quantity Does Not Match

pages.html:
VunaPOS supports both manual and automatic allocation of batches and serial numbers for stock-tracked items.

This ensures that invoices are submitted using valid inventory records from the warehouse configured in the active POS Profile.

Batch and serial allocation is handled before checkout so that the cashier can identify stock problems early rather than discovering them after payment has already been collected.

Requirements

Before using batch or serial allocation in VunaPOS:

  1. Enable batch or serial number tracking on the ERPNext Item.
  2. Create the required Batch or Serial No records.
  3. Ensure stock is available in the warehouse configured in the POS Profile.
  4. Confirm that the batch is not expired.
  5. Confirm that the serial number is available for delivery.
  6. Confirm the item's stock UOM and the conversion factor for the selling UOM.

VunaPOS uses ERPNext stock records as the source of truth.

Invoices versus orders

These allocation rules apply when issuing stock on an invoice. Ordinary retail Sales Orders do not require stock/batch/serial allocation merely to record the order. Switching an Order cart to Invoice restores invoice validation.

Restaurant kitchen orders are different: prepared items check/reserve recipe ingredients and manufactured output. See Configure Kitchen Preparation.

Example: cartons and pieces

One carton contains 24 pieces. Selling one carton requires 24 pieces of batch allocation, not one. Selling two cartons and three pieces on separate lines uses 51 pieces of the same warehouse stock in total.

[Screenshot: Cart line showing 1 Carton with conversion factor 24 and batch allocations totalling 24 Pcs]

Batch-Tracked Items

A batch-tracked item represents stock grouped under a Batch number.

This is commonly used for:

  • food products
  • medicines
  • cosmetics
  • chemicals
  • manufactured goods
  • items with expiry dates

When a batch-tracked item is added to the cart, VunaPOS must identify which batch quantities will be delivered.

Automatic Batch Allocation

VunaPOS by default selects valid batches without requiring the cashier to choose them manually.

The allocation follows a First Expiry, First Out approach where applicable.

This means VunaPOS prioritises:

  1. Non-expired batches
  2. Batches with the earliest expiry date
  3. Older batches when expiry dates are equal

Expired batches and batches with no available quantity are ignored.

Multi-Batch Allocation

VunaPOS can distribute the requested quantity across several batches.

For example:

Requested Quantity: 5

Batch A: 2
Batch B: 3

VunaPOS allocates:

Batch A × 2
Batch B × 3

The sale can continue because the total valid batch stock satisfies the requested quantity.

This is useful where no single batch has enough stock but the combined available quantity is sufficient.

Manual Batch Allocation

Manual allocation allows the cashier to select the exact batch or batches that should be used.

Use manual allocation when:

  • the customer requests stock from a specific batch
  • staff need to prioritise a particular batch
  • the automatically suggested allocation should be changed
  • physical stock at the counter differs from the suggested selection

To allocate batches manually:

  1. Add the batch-tracked item to the cart.
  2. Open the batch allocation control on the cart item.
  3. Review the available batches and quantities.
  4. Select one or more batches.
  5. Enter the quantity to take from each batch.
  6. Confirm the allocation.

The total quantity allocated across batches must equal the quantity being sold in stock UOM.

For example:

Cart Quantity: 6 stock units

Batch A: 4
Batch B: 2

The allocation is valid because:

4 + 2 = 6

VunaPOS prevents checkout when the manually allocated quantity does not match the cart quantity.

Serialised Items

A serialised item is tracked using a unique Serial Number for each physical unit.

This is commonly used for:

  • phones
  • laptops
  • appliances
  • machinery
  • electronics
  • equipment requiring warranty tracking

Each unit sold must have a valid and available Serial Number.

If the cart represents three stock units, exactly three Serial Numbers must be allocated. Selling-unit conversions must be included when finding that stock quantity.

Automatic Serial Number Allocation

When VunaPOS allocates Serial Numbers automatically, it selects available units from the configured warehouse.

For example:

Requested Quantity: 3

VunaPOS may allocate:

SN-00041
SN-00042
SN-00043

The allocated Serial Numbers are attached to the invoice item before submission.

VunaPOS only selects Serial Numbers that are available for delivery from the active warehouse.

Manual Serial Number Allocation

Manual allocation allows the cashier to select the exact units being sold.

This is useful where the cashier is scanning or physically handling a specific device or product.

To allocate Serial Numbers manually:

  1. Add the serialised item to the cart.
  2. Open the serial number allocation control.
  3. Enter/select the required Serial Numbers using the allocation control.
  4. Confirm the selection.

The number of selected Serial Numbers must match the cart's stock-unit quantity.

For example:

Cart Quantity: 2

Selected Serial Numbers:
SN-00051
SN-00052

This is valid because two Serial Numbers have been selected for a quantity of two.

Barcode Scanning

Where batch or serial identifiers are represented by barcodes, the cashier can scan them during manual allocation.

The scanned value may identify:

  • an Item
  • a Batch
  • a Serial Number

VunaPOS uses the scanned identifier to locate the matching stock record and apply it to the cart item where valid.

Unknown, unavailable, or invalid identifiers are rejected.

Cart Display

After allocation, the cart shows the selected batch or serial details.

A batch-tracked item may display:

Batches:
BATCH-A × 2
BATCH-B × 3

A serialised item may display:

Serial Numbers:
SN-00041
SN-00042

This allows the cashier to review the allocation before proceeding to checkout.

Changing Item Quantity

If the cart quantity changes, VunaPOS revalidates the current allocation.

For batch items:

  • increasing quantity may require additional batch stock
  • reducing quantity may reduce or rebuild the allocation

For serialised items:

  • increasing quantity requires additional Serial Numbers
  • reducing quantity removes unnecessary Serial Numbers from the allocation

The cashier should review the resulting allocation before checkout.

Checkout Validation

Before submitting the invoice, VunaPOS checks that:

  • every batch-tracked item has a valid allocation
  • allocated batch quantities match the invoice's stock-unit quantity
  • allocated batches are not expired
  • sufficient batch stock is still available
  • every serialised item has the required number of Serial Numbers
  • selected Serial Numbers are available in the correct warehouse

Checkout is blocked when any allocation is missing or invalid.

This final validation protects against stock changes that may occur between adding the item and completing the sale.

What Happens on the Invoice

When the sale is completed, VunaPOS attaches the selected batch and serial information to the relevant invoice rows.

Depending on the installed ERPNext version and stock configuration, this may use an ERPNext Serial and Batch Bundle.

The submitted Sales Invoice or POS Invoice remains the source of truth for:

  • delivered batches
  • delivered Serial Numbers
  • warehouse deductions
  • Stock Ledger entries
  • item traceability

VunaPOS does not maintain a separate batch or serial inventory ledger.

Example: Automatic Batch Allocation

Example: Manual Serial Allocation

Important Notes

Note: Automatic allocation is intended to reduce cashier effort, but the resulting allocation should still be visible before checkout.

Note: Manual selection is useful when the physical item being handed to the customer must match a specific batch or Serial Number.

Warning: Batch and serial availability can change when another user submits a transaction. VunaPOS validates the allocation again during checkout.

Warning: Expired batches cannot be selected for a normal sale.

Common Problems

Insufficient Batch Stock

Cause

The total quantity available across valid batches is lower than the quantity being sold.

Resolution

  1. Reduce the cart quantity.
  2. Review stock in the POS Profile warehouse.
  3. Transfer or receive additional stock.
  4. Retry the allocation.

Allocated Batch Quantity Does Not Match

Cause

The allocation does not equal the required stock-unit quantity. Check the selling UOM and its conversion factor.

Resolution

  1. Review each selected batch.
  2. Adjust the allocated quantities.
  3. Ensure their total equals quantity × conversion factor, in stock UOM.
  4. Confirm the allocation again.

Expired Batch Cannot Be Selected

Cause

The selected batch has passed its expiry date.

Resolution

  1. Choose another valid batch.
  2. Review the Batch record in ERPNext.
  3. Correct the expiry date only if the record itself is incorrect.

Not Enough Serial Numbers

Cause

There are fewer available Serial Numbers than the requested item quantity.

Resolution

  1. Reduce the cart quantity.
  2. Check Serial Number availability in the selected warehouse.
  3. Transfer the required serialised stock.
  4. Retry the sale.

Serial Number Is Unavailable

Cause

The Serial Number may already have been delivered, reserved, or stored in another warehouse.

Resolution

  1. Search for the Serial Number in ERPNext.
  2. Confirm its current warehouse and status.
  3. Select another available Serial Number.

Allocation Changed Before Checkout

Cause

Another stock transaction may have used the selected batch or Serial Number before the sale was submitted.

Resolution

  1. Review the allocation error.
  2. Refresh or reopen the allocation selector.
  3. Allow VunaPOS to allocate again or choose another stock record.
  4. Retry checkout.

pages.title: Pause and Resume Draft Invoices
pages.html:
Use Hold when an invoice is intentionally unfinished—for example, the customer needs to fetch another item. Holding is not payment or submission.

Save and find a draft

  1. Build the cart with the correct customer, units and quantities.
  2. Select Hold.
  3. Confirm it was saved before leaving the page.
  4. Open Sales History → Draft Invoices and use the available search/filters to find it.

This tab shows invoice drafts, not Sales Orders. Use Draft Orders for retail Sales Order drafts.

Continue the sale

Open the row to inspect its details. Choose Edit to restore the draft to the cart, or Checkout when no further editing is required. Review customer, shipping address, prices and batch/serial allocation before completing payment.

The original “held” marker stays on an intentionally held invoice even after editing or submission. A submitted held invoice is no longer an unfinished draft; look in Sales History for the completed transaction.

Opening Checkout alone does not complete the invoice. If you leave or refresh before confirming, look for the saved draft before creating a replacement.

What is not saved

An unsaved cart is not protected simply because it is on screen. Refreshing, pulling to refresh on mobile or clearing the cart can lose unsaved work. Hold it first.

A background-submission failure is not the same as an intentionally held invoice. Review its submission state using Connection and Submission Recovery.

[Screenshot: Draft Invoices list filters and an opened draft with Edit and Checkout actions]

pages.title: Create and Manage Sales Orders
pages.html:
Use a Sales Order when the customer is ordering now but delivery and invoicing happen later.

This page covers the retail Order option. Restaurant Place Order is a different workflow with kitchen preparation; see Restaurant Overview.

Create the order

  1. Select Order in the transaction-type selector, if the profile permits changing it.
  2. Confirm customer, shipping address and price list.
  3. Add items, variants, selling UOMs and quantities.
  4. Open Checkout, set the delivery date and complete any required fields.
  5. Review and complete the order, or follow its approval workflow.

A normal retail Sales Order does not issue stock. Out-of-stock items, including variants, can be ordered; batch and serial allocation is not required just to place it. If you switch the cart back to Invoice, invoice stock and tracking checks apply.

Deposits

When Allow Sales Order Advance Payments is enabled, the cashier can collect an order advance during checkout using permitted payment methods. Otherwise an order can be placed without pretending that it has been paid.

An advance is not proof of delivery and does not make the order an invoice. Use the order and its linked payment information when checking what the customer paid; Sales Orders do not use invoice-style outstanding balances.

Find and edit

Open Sales History. Use Sales Orders for submitted/cancelled orders and Draft Orders for drafts awaiting completion or approval. Open the row to review its status and available actions.

Use Edit where offered. The restored cart must remain in Sales Order context with its customer. Submitted restaurant rounds cannot be edited this way.

Workflow actions and permissions may restrict editing. Do not replace a submitted order with an invoice merely to bypass approval.

Fulfil later

Use your organisation's normal ERPNext delivery/invoicing process against the Sales Order. VunaPOS does not turn order placement into a dispatch-tracking service.

[Screenshot: Order checkout showing delivery date and optional advance-payment section]

[Video: Creating a Sales Order with zero warehouse stock, finding it in Sales History and editing an eligible draft]

pages.title: Customer Loyalty Points

headings.title: Loyalty Redemption Exceeds the Sale Amount

pages.html:
VunaPOS supports ERPNext Loyalty Program directly within the POS checkout flow.

When a customer enrolled in a Loyalty Program is selected, VunaPOS displays the customer’s available loyalty points and allows the cashier to redeem those points during checkout.

This makes it possible to reward repeat customers without leaving the POS or manually adjusting the invoice.

Requirements

Before loyalty points can be used in VunaPOS:

  1. Create and configure a Loyalty Program in ERPNext.
  2. Enroll the customer in the Loyalty Program.
  3. Ensure the customer has earned loyalty points.
  4. Confirm the selected customer is not the default walk-in customer unless that customer is intentionally enrolled.

VunaPOS reads loyalty information from ERPNext. It does not maintain a separate loyalty balance.

View Customer Loyalty Points

To view available loyalty points:

  1. Open VunaPOS.
  2. Select a customer enrolled in a Loyalty Program.
  3. Add items to the cart.
  4. Open Checkout.

VunaPOS displays the customer’s current loyalty points in the checkout page.

The displayed balance helps the cashier confirm whether the customer has enough points to redeem against the sale.

Selected Customer with loyalty points

Redeem Loyalty Points

To redeem points during checkout:

  1. Select an enrolled customer.
  2. Add the required items to the cart.
  3. Click Checkout.
  4. Review the customer’s available loyalty points.
  5. Enter or select the number of points to redeem.
  6. Confirm the loyalty redemption value.
  7. Select a Mode of Payment for any remaining amount.
  8. Complete the sale.

The loyalty redemption reduces the amount the customer needs to pay using Cash, M-Pesa, Card, or another Mode of Payment.

For example:

Grand Total: KES 1,300.00
Loyalty Redemption: KES 300.00
Amount Remaining: KES 1,000.00

The cashier then records payment for the remaining KES 1,000.00.

Redeeming Loyalty points in checkout page

Checkout Behaviour

When loyalty points are entered, VunaPOS validates the redemption before completing the sale.

The sale cannot be completed when:

  • the customer is not enrolled in a Loyalty Program
  • the customer does not have enough points
  • the entered points exceed the available balance
  • the redemption value exceeds the allowed amount
  • the remaining payment amount does not match the invoice balance

The checkout page should always show the final amount remaining after loyalty redemption.

What Happens on the Invoice

When the sale is completed, VunaPOS submits the required Sales Invoice or POS Invoice with the loyalty redemption information.

ERPNext remains the source of truth for:

  • available loyalty points
  • redeemed points
  • loyalty redemption amount
  • points earned from the completed sale
  • the customer’s updated loyalty balance

VunaPOS does not maintain a separate loyalty ledger.

Important Notes

Note: Loyalty points are customer-specific. Make sure the correct customer is selected before redeeming points.

Note: The redemption value depends on the Loyalty Program configuration in ERPNext.

Warning: Do not change the customer after loyalty points have been applied without recalculating the checkout.

Common Problems

Loyalty Points Are Not Displayed

Cause

The selected customer may not be enrolled in a Loyalty Program, or the customer may not have earned any points.

Resolution

  1. Open the customer in ERPNext.
  2. Confirm the customer is enrolled in a Loyalty Program.
  3. Check the customer’s available loyalty points.
  4. Return to VunaPOS and select the customer again.

The Customer Has Insufficient Points

Cause

The entered redemption amount requires more points than the customer currently has.

Resolution

  1. Review the available points shown in checkout.
  2. Reduce the number of points being redeemed.
  3. Use another Mode of Payment for the remaining amount.

Loyalty Redemption Exceeds the Sale Amount

Cause

The redemption value is greater than the invoice amount allowed for loyalty redemption.

Resolution

  1. Reduce the number of points entered.
  2. Confirm the remaining balance.
  3. Complete payment using the available payment methods.

Loyalty Balance Did Not Update

Cause

The invoice may not have submitted successfully, or ERPNext may not have completed the loyalty posting.

Resolution

  1. Confirm the Sales Invoice or POS Invoice is submitted.
  2. Review the loyalty information on the invoice.
  3. Check the customer’s Loyalty Point Entry records in ERPNext.
  4. Reload the customer in VunaPOS.

pages.title: Return Items from a Sale
pages.html:
Use a return against the original submitted invoice when goods are being returned. Do not enter a new negative retail sale as a substitute.

Before starting

The profile must permit Allow Returns, your user must be allowed to create/submit the relevant return, and you need an open POS shift and a server connection. The original must be an eligible VunaPOS invoice for this profile, not a Sales Order, another credit note or an unsubmitted draft.

Process the return

  1. Find the original invoice in Sales History and open it.
  2. Select Return items.
  3. Review sold, previously returned and remaining returnable quantities.
  4. Enter the quantities being returned, or use Return all available items.
  5. Enter the return reason.
  6. Review and submit the return using the available action.

Quantities are against the original invoice rows and units. You cannot return more than remains returnable. Two rows of the same item may represent different units; choose the correct row.

The resulting return/credit note stays linked to the original sale and appears under Returns and credit notes in invoice details.

Refunds and tracked stock

Review the resulting credit note and payment treatment with your accounts policy, especially when the original used several payment methods. Recording a return does not promise that an external mobile-money/card provider has sent a refund.

ERPNext's stock and batch/serial rules still apply. If a return cannot be submitted because of tracking, period locks or permissions, ask an authorised stock/accounts user to resolve it in ERPNext. Do not record a second return while the first outcome is unclear.

[Screenshot: Return items dialog showing sold, returned and returnable quantities with a required reason]

pages.title: Cash, Split Payments and Credit Sales

headings.title: Pay with one or several methods

pages.html:
Use checkout to settle a new sale. Use Receiving and Reconciling Payments when collecting an old balance or a customer advance.

Pay with one or several methods

  1. Review the final total after taxes, delivery charges and any loyalty redemption.
  2. Enter the amount for each payment method being used.
  3. Check the allocated, remaining and change amounts.
  4. Verify any integrated gateway amount before completing the sale.

For example, a KES 1,000 sale can be allocated as Cash 400 and Card 600. Do not enter the whole total against both rows. A cash amount above the sale may produce change; do not assume overpayments on every other method are accepted as cash change.

When Automatically Allocate Payment Balance is enabled, the remaining amount can be assigned to an eligible manual method while entering payments. Review the result; gateway payments still need actual verification.

Payment methods and company accounts come from the profile. The default method is not the only method you may use.

Leave a customer balance

Use a credit sale only when Allow Credit Sales is enabled and the customer is allowed to buy on account.

  1. Select the correct named customer.
  2. Open checkout and enable the credit-sale option.
  3. Confirm the due date.
  4. Record any payment actually collected now.
  5. Review the unpaid balance and complete the sale or its approval step.

Do not allocate an unpaid amount to a made-up “Credit” payment method. The invoice balance is what the customer still owes. Standard ERPNext credit/accounting checks can still reject the sale.

A profile's Default Sale Type can start checkout as Cash Sale or Credit Sale, but review it for the customer in front of you.

Order deposits are different

A Sales Order advance requires Allow Sales Order Advance Payments. It is a payment against an order, not an invoice outstanding balance. See Sales Orders.

Delivery amounts

Where Allow Delivery Charges is configured, review the delivery amount in checkout. Changing it is possible only when the profile allows it. The amount is represented using the configured service item and affects the official totals.

An address and a delivery charge do not assign a driver or confirm delivery.

[Screenshot: Checkout allocating one sale across Cash and Card, with allocated and remaining totals]

[Screenshot: Credit-sale checkout showing due date and the unpaid balance]

pages.title: M-Pesa Integration

headings.title: If the customer paid but checkout failed

pages.html:
Use integrated M-Pesa checkout when your site can verify the provider's payment before completing the sale. A manually configured payment method called M-Pesa is not automatically an STK/C2B integration.

Before using the integration

Ask the administrator to configure the supported payment connector, its gateway account, company/currency and provider credentials/callbacks. Current deployments use Vuna Payments; older configuration and some messages use the name navari_ke_payments. The connector must provide the site's payment-request and C2B-register functionality.

Link the appropriate Payment Gateway Account on the relevant payment row in the POS Profile. A company ledger account on Mode of Payment is also required. Test provider confirmation before giving cashiers access.

Without a connector you can still record a manual M-Pesa payment according to your business's verification procedure, but VunaPOS cannot send STK prompts or search provider transactions for that manual row.

Collect an STK payment

  1. Open checkout and select the gateway-linked M-Pesa payment method.
  2. Allocate the intended amount to that payment method. Check the total before sending a prompt.
  3. Open STK Push, confirm the customer's phone number and select Send STK.
  4. Ask the customer to approve the prompt on their phone.
  5. Wait for the payment status to update. Use the status-check action if it remains pending.
  6. Use the verified payment in checkout, then complete the sale.

Sending the prompt is not proof of payment. A pending, failed or expired request must not be recorded as a successful gateway payment. Keep the same checkout open while checking a delayed result; do not send another prompt just because a response is slow.

The customer-facing reference uses the available invoice/order reference, rather than a retry key. Where no document reference is available, a VUNAPOS label may be used.

Use an existing C2B payment

  1. Select C2B Payment in the gateway dialog.
  2. Search for the provider transaction using the available phone/reference information.
  3. Confirm that the transaction, amount and currency match the customer and this sale.
  4. Select/attach the matching payment and use it in checkout.
  5. Complete the sale after successful verification.

A transaction already consumed, reconciled or reserved for another checkout cannot simply be attached again. A match in search is not permission to use somebody else's payment.

If the customer paid but checkout failed

Check the payment status and the invoice/order result before taking more money. Keep the transaction reference and ask the cashier/accounts lead to investigate an already-used or unavailable payment. Cancelling a payment selection or allowing it to expire is not a refund from the provider.

For sale checkout, the verified reference is attached to the invoice payment. Receiving money through the separate Payments page creates an ERPNext Payment Entry; see Receiving and Reconciling Payments.

[Video: Sending an STK prompt, waiting for provider confirmation and completing checkout without sending a second prompt]

[Screenshot: C2B lookup showing a matching amount, transaction reference and payment status]

pages.title: Receiving and Reconciling Payments

headings.title: Receive an advance or check a receipt
Payment Amount Exceeds the Selected Invoices
Invoice Still Shows an Outstanding Balance
User Cannot Receive or Reconcile Payments

pages.html:
VunaPOS allows authorised users to receive customer payments and reconcile them against outstanding invoices without leaving the POS workspace.

This is useful when a customer returns to pay an existing balance, settles several invoices at once, or makes a payment that must later be matched to the correct ERPNext transaction.

VunaPOS uses ERPNext payment and reconciliation records as the source of truth. It does not maintain a separate payment ledger.

Requirements

Before receiving or reconciling payments in VunaPOS:

  1. Configure the required Modes of Payment in ERPNext.
  2. Assign the correct company accounts to each Mode of Payment.
  3. Ensure the user has permission to create payments.
  4. Ensure the user has permission to view and reconcile customer invoices.
  5. For invoice settlement, confirm the customer has a submitted invoice with an outstanding balance. An advance can be received without selecting an invoice.

Where gateway payments such as M-Pesa are used, the relevant payment integration must also be installed and configured.

Receiving a Payment

Use Receive Payment when a customer is paying an existing outstanding balance rather than completing a new POS sale.

To receive a payment:

  1. Open Payments from the VunaPOS sidebar.
  2. Open the Receive tab.
  3. Select the customer.
  4. Review the customer’s outstanding invoices.
  5. Select the invoice under Apply to invoice, or leave it empty for a customer advance.
  6. Choose a Mode of Payment.
  7. Enter the payment amount.
  8. Add the payment reference where required.
  9. Review the allocation.
  10. Select Receive and allocate payment or Receive customer advance, as appropriate.

VunaPOS creates the appropriate ERPNext payment record and links the payment to the selected invoices.

Selecting Outstanding Invoices

After selecting a customer, VunaPOS displays invoices that still have an outstanding balance.

The list may include:

  • invoice number
  • posting date
  • grand total
  • paid amount
  • outstanding amount
  • due date
  • payment status

When receiving a payment, select the invoice under Apply to invoice, or receive
the amount as a customer advance. Use Reconcile to distribute existing available
payments/credits across several invoices.

For example:

Customer: Acme Traders

ACC-SINV-2026-00120
Outstanding: KES 4,000.00

ACC-SINV-2026-00137
Outstanding: KES 2,500.00

If the customer pays KES 6,500.00 as an advance, use Reconcile to preview and apply
that available payment across both invoices.

Partial Payments

VunaPOS can receive a payment that settles only part of an invoice where partial payment is allowed.

For example:

Invoice Outstanding: KES 10,000.00
Payment Received: KES 4,000.00
Remaining Balance: KES 6,000.00

The invoice remains outstanding for the unpaid balance.

The remaining amount can be collected through another payment later.

Unallocated Payments

A customer may make a payment before the exact invoice allocation is known.

Where supported by the configured ERPNext workflow, the payment can remain partly or fully unallocated.

For example:

Payment Received: KES 10,000.00
Allocated: KES 7,500.00
Unallocated: KES 2,500.00

The remaining amount can later be reconciled against another invoice.

Note: Whether unallocated payments are permitted depends on the accounting rules and permissions configured in ERPNext.

Receive an advance or check a receipt

Leave Apply to invoice empty when receiving a customer advance. The submitted payment keeps an unallocated balance that can later be matched to compatible invoices.

Open History to search the payment records you are permitted to see. Open the receipt/print action where available. Keep the receipt number when a customer later asks how the money was allocated.

Payments are online-only. Profile switches for customer payments, reconciliation and payment history may hide the corresponding tabs.

Payment References

Some Modes of Payment require a transaction reference.

Examples include:

  • M-Pesa transaction ID
  • bank reference
  • card authorisation code
  • cheque number
  • deposit slip number

Enter the reference before confirming the payment where required.

Payment references help with:

  • reconciliation
  • audit
  • duplicate-payment checks
  • customer enquiries
  • bank and gateway matching

Payment Reconciliation

Payment reconciliation links an existing payment to one or more outstanding invoices.

Use reconciliation when:

  • a payment was received without an invoice allocation
  • the customer paid before an invoice was created
  • a bank or mobile-money transaction must be matched later
  • several payments and invoices need to be matched

To reconcile a payment:

  1. Open Payments.
  2. Select the Reconcile tab.
  3. Select the customer.
  4. Review available payments.
  5. Review outstanding invoices.
  6. Select the payment to reconcile.
  7. Select the invoice or invoices to apply it against.
  8. Select Allocate to calculate an allocation preview.
  9. Review the proposed allocations and remaining balances.
  10. Select Reconcile to apply the reviewed allocation.

After reconciliation, ERPNext updates the linked invoices and payment allocations.

Reconciliation Example

Matching Payments

Before applying a payment, confirm that the following details match:

  • customer
  • company
  • currency
  • payment amount
  • transaction reference
  • payment date
  • Mode of Payment

VunaPOS should prevent reconciliation where the customer, company, or currency is incompatible with the selected invoice.

M-Pesa Payments

Where the site's supported payments connector is installed and configured, M-Pesa can be verified when receiving money. See M-Pesa Integration.

A transaction can be identified using details such as:

  • M-Pesa transaction ID
  • phone number
  • customer
  • amount
  • transaction date
  • payment status

The selected payment is then applied to the appropriate invoice through the normal reconciliation process.

Note: Receiving or selecting an M-Pesa transaction does not replace ERPNext payment allocation. The payment must still be linked to the appropriate invoice where required.

What Happens in ERPNext

When a payment is received, VunaPOS creates an ERPNext payment entry record.

When reconciliation is completed, ERPNext records the relationship between:

  • the customer payment
  • the selected invoice or invoices
  • the allocated amount
  • any remaining unallocated amount

ERPNext remains responsible for:

  • receivable balances
  • invoice outstanding amounts
  • General Ledger entries
  • payment references
  • reconciliation history
  • customer account balances

VunaPOS provides the interface for completing these actions from the POS workspace.

Permissions

Payment receipt and reconciliation should be restricted to authorised users.

A cashier may be allowed to receive payments but not modify previous allocations.

The profile controls access to receipt, reconciliation and history. ERPNext permissions still apply. Correcting already-posted allocations may require a separate authorised ERPNext accounting procedure; the POS Reconcile tab is not a general-purpose undo tool.

Configure the required ERPNext roles and permissions according to your organisation’s controls.

Important Notes

Note: Always select the correct customer before receiving or reconciling a payment.

Note: The total amount allocated across invoices cannot exceed the payment amount.

Warning: Confirm the transaction reference before saving. Duplicate or incorrect references can make reconciliation and audit difficult.

Warning: Reallocating a submitted payment may require additional permissions and should follow the organisation’s accounting controls.

Common Problems

No Outstanding Invoices Are Displayed

Cause

The selected customer may not have any submitted invoices with an outstanding balance.

Resolution

  1. Confirm the selected customer.
  2. Check the customer’s invoices in ERPNext.
  3. Confirm the invoice is submitted.
  4. Confirm the invoice still has an outstanding amount.
  5. Reload the payment screen.

Payment Amount Exceeds the Selected Invoices

Cause

The amount allocated is greater than the combined outstanding balance of the selected invoices.

Resolution

  1. Review the invoice balances.
  2. Reduce the allocated amount.
  3. Leave the remaining amount unallocated where allowed.
  4. Confirm the payment again.

Payment Cannot Be Reconciled

Cause

The payment and invoice may belong to different customers, companies, or currencies.

Resolution

  1. Confirm the customer on both records.
  2. Confirm the company.
  3. Confirm the transaction currency.
  4. Select compatible records and retry.

Transaction Reference Already Exists

Cause

The payment reference may already have been used on another payment.

Resolution

  1. Verify the reference from the payment provider or receipt.
  2. Search for the existing payment.
  3. Do not create a duplicate payment.
  4. Reconcile the existing record where appropriate.

Invoice Still Shows an Outstanding Balance

Cause

The payment may not have been fully allocated, or the allocated amount may be lower than the invoice balance.

Resolution

  1. Open the payment allocation.
  2. Review the amount applied to the invoice.
  3. Confirm the payment was submitted successfully.
  4. Reconcile any remaining amount.

User Cannot Receive or Reconcile Payments

Cause

The user may not have the required ERPNext permissions.

Resolution

  1. Review the user’s assigned roles.
  2. Confirm permission to create the relevant payment record.
  3. Confirm permission to view invoices and perform reconciliation.
  4. Ask a system administrator to update the permissions where necessary.

pages.title: Print Receipts
pages.html:
Use the saved transaction to print a receipt or invoice. A printed page is not proof that an unsubmitted draft has been approved.

Print a completed sale

  1. Confirm the completed transaction and its invoice number.
  2. Use the print action offered after checkout, or open the transaction from Sales History and choose its print action.
  3. Review the rendered document, then use the browser's print dialog.
  4. Select the intended printer, paper size and scaling.

ERPNext Print Formats control the layout. Ask the administrator to select a format compatible with the document type and your thermal/A4 paper. A label such as “POS Receipt” is an example of a site's custom format, not a format every installation necessarily has.

Reprint a payment receipt

Open Payments → History, find the payment and use the available receipt action. Check the receipt number, customer and allocated amounts before giving it to the customer.

If printing does not work

  • Allow the requested print window if the browser blocks it.
  • Confirm the transaction is available to your user.
  • Check the printer connection, paper and browser settings.
  • Ask the administrator to inspect the Print Format if content is cut off or totals/details are missing.

VunaPOS does not guarantee silent printing or automatic routing to a physical kitchen printer. The Restaurant kitchen workflow uses the KDS; do not assume opening a kitchen ticket sends paper to a station printer.

[Screenshot: Invoice receipt preview beside the browser print dialog configured for thermal paper]

pages.title: Restaurant Overview

headings.title: A visit is not a shift

pages.html:
