Restaurant mode uses the familiar VunaPOS selling screen to manage a guest visit from ordering to kitchen preparation and billing.

Who does what?

Person Normal task
Restaurant manager Sets up location, menus, tables, kitchens and staff access; handles exceptions.
Waiter Opens a shift, selects a service/table, places orders and adds later rounds.
Chef / kitchen operator Uses the kitchen display to accept, prepare and mark tickets ready.
Cashier Opens a shift, finds the visit and collects payment for its bill.

These can be separate users on separate terminals. They must be assigned to appropriate profiles in the same Restaurant/Branch and have the required roles/record access. They do not need to share a login.

A visit is not a shift

A POS shift belongs to a staff member. A restaurant visit/session belongs to the guest party and its tables or table-free service.

One visit can have several ordering rounds. Each placed round becomes a saved Sales Order. Kitchen-routed lines produce kitchen order tickets (KOTs), grouped by station. At billing, the visit's eligible unbilled rounds become one invoice.

Normal sequence:

  1. Waiter opens a visit and selects the table for dine-in.
  2. Waiter selects menu items and Place Order.
  3. Chef sees the KOT and progresses preparation.
  4. Waiter can add another round to the same visit.
  5. Cashier bills the visit and completes payment/approval as required.
  6. Successful settlement releases the tables.

[Diagram: Waiter places a round → station KOT → chef marks Ready → waiter serves → cashier bills the visit]

Shared tools, purposeful differences

Customers, addresses, taxes, checkout fields and payment methods use the shared POS tools. Restaurant mode adds Service Type, Floor, Open Orders and Kitchen.

A restaurant Service Type, such as Dine In or Takeaway, describes how the visit is served. It is not the retail Invoice/Order selector. Placing a restaurant order is not taking payment.

Know the current boundaries

  • One bill per visit; there is no seat-level split-bill workflow in this module.
  • Guest count and table seats are available, not individual guest/seat tracking.
  • Menu Sections/Courses organize browsing; they do not schedule course firing.
  • A table-free service can be named Delivery, but this does not provide drivers, dispatch tracking or aggregator integration.
  • Prepared items use real ERPNext BOM/Work Order and stock checks. They are not ordinary stock-free retail Sales Orders.
  • The KDS is the kitchen workflow; automatic physical kitchen-printer routing is not implied.

Start with Set Up a Restaurant, or go to Take Dine-in and Takeaway Orders if your manager has finished setup.

pages.title: Set Up a Restaurant

headings.title: 1. Prepare the company and stock locations
4. Prepare items, prices and a menu

pages.html:
Use this guide to prepare a new restaurant location. Start with a small working menu and test waiter, chef and cashier accounts before loading the full operation.

1. Prepare the company and stock locations

Complete the standard counter setup: Company, accounts, tax templates, selling price list, payment accounts and a default customer.

Choose the warehouse from which completed dishes and direct-sale products will be sold. Configure raw-material and optional work-in-progress warehouses for the kitchens. These must belong to the same Company.

Enable Stock Reservation in Stock Settings for stock-bearing restaurant orders.
Have stock/manufacturing staff prepare real recipes and ingredient balances
before the first service.

2. Identify the restaurant and branch

Create/select the ERPNext Branch and set its Company. Create Restaurant with its name, Company and enabled status.

Restaurant and Branch are independent records. A Restaurant can operate across several branches of its Company; a branch is not owned by a single Restaurant record. Operational records pair the two. Use that same Restaurant/Branch pair on profiles, floors and kitchen stations.

Leave Default Menu blank until the menu exists, then return and select it. You do not need a second Restaurant named after every floor.

3. Decide which services you offer

Configure Restaurant Service Type for Dine In, Takeaway or your business's equivalent labels:

  • Enable Requires Table for dine-in.
  • Leave it off for table-free service.
  • Use Display Order to control the selection order.
  • Add a service-specific Price List or tax template only when it should override the normal transaction pricing.

In Restaurant → Service Types, add rows in the order Service Type, Branch, Default:

  • Leave Branch blank for services offered by branches without their own list.
  • To give a branch its own list, select that Branch on every service it should offer.
    This list replaces the blank-Branch rows for that branch; it does not add to them.
  • Select one Default per branch, and one for the blank-Branch list. If none is
    selected, the first enabled service in Display Order is selected automatically.
  • You can repeat a service for different branches, but not twice for the same
    branch or twice with Branch blank. Branch must belong to the Restaurant's Company.

For example, offer Dine In and Takeaway with Branch blank, then add only Takeaway
for Meru. Meru offers Takeaway only; Nairobi uses Dine In and Takeaway unless it
has its own rows. Every POS Profile with the same Restaurant/Branch uses that list.

Disabled service types are never offered. If a branch's list contains only disabled
services, it does not fall back to the shared list. A branch without its own rows
or blank-Branch rows has no offered services once the Restaurant has service
assignments. If the entire Service Types table is empty, all enabled service types
remain available; configure explicit rows to restrict them.

Avoid offering a label that staff cannot actually fulfil. A service named Delivery
is a table-free ordering choice, not a delivery-management system.

[Screenshot: Restaurant Service Types showing blank-Branch Dine In and Takeaway rows, a Meru Takeaway row, and defaults for each scope]

4. Prepare items, prices and a menu

Create sales Items and Item Prices. Configure Menu Section records, then Restaurant Menu items with a Section/Course and availability.

Select the menu as the Restaurant's default. For branch/floor menus, follow Build Menus and Item Choices. Menu sections organize selling; Item Groups route kitchen work.

5. Configure the restaurant counter

In POS Profile:

  1. Set POS Mode to Restaurant.
  2. Select Restaurant and Restaurant Branch, matching the profile Company.
  3. Confirm the selling warehouse, currency, selling price list, customer, taxes and payment accounts.
  4. Add each operating user under the profile's user assignments.
  5. Enable only the customer/payment and approval options the counter needs.

Company, warehouse and accounting defaults stay on the profile; do not recreate them as separate outlet settings.

A profile with restaurant transaction history cannot simply be moved to another Restaurant/Branch. Create another profile for a different operating location.

6. Arrange tables and kitchens

After the profile exists, managers can use Floor → Floor Editor to build the plan. Floors and tables can also be maintained in Desk; floors are paired to Restaurant/Branch and tables inherit them.

Then complete Configure Kitchen Preparation, including recipes and ingredient stock. Apply floor-specific menus/stations after the floors exist.

[Diagram: Company → Restaurant and Branch context; Items/Prices → Menu; POS Profile → Floor Editor; Floors + Item Groups + preparation warehouses → Kitchen Stations]

7. Assign staff roles and access

Role Use it for
VunaPOS Restaurant Manager Restaurant setup and management actions.
VunaPOS Waiter Guest visits, ordering and serving.
VunaPOS Kitchen User KDS preparation actions.
VunaPOS Cashier Billing and collecting restaurant payments.

Users may hold more than one role when your business needs it. Kitchen-only users open directly into kitchen functions and need no selling shift. Waiters and cashiers open separate shifts even on the same profile.

Assign the relevant profile and standard permissions. Optional Branch and Kitchen Station User Permissions restrict records further; they are not mandatory for every installation. Do not grant accounting/manufacturing administration to every chef just to use KDS.

8. Rehearse a visit

On separate browser profiles/devices: waiter opens a shift and places an order; chef opens KDS and prepares it; cashier opens their own shift and bills the same visit. Confirm prices, stock movements, receipt and table release.

[Video: First restaurant test with separate waiter, chef and cashier logins]

pages.title: Build Menus and Item Choices

headings.title: Configure modifiers and add-ons on Item

pages.html:
Use menus to decide what staff can order and how they browse it. Keep selling prices in ERPNext Item Price/Pricing Rules rather than treating the menu as another price list.

Organize the menu

  1. Create enabled Menu Sections, such as Breakfast, Main Dishes and Drinks. Display Order controls their browsing order.
  2. Create the required Items, UOMs and selling prices.
  3. Open Restaurant Menu, enter its name and choose any Company/Restaurant scope needed.
  4. Add each Item or variant template under Items and select its Section/Course.
  5. Leave Available enabled for orderable items; clear it to stop ordering that menu item temporarily.
  6. Enable/save the menu and assign the shared default on Restaurant if required.

The same item should appear once in the menu. Choose the actual variant when ordering from a template. A Section/Course is not a kitchen destination or an automatic instruction to fire a course later.

Shared, branch and floor menus

  • Default: select the shared menu as Restaurant's Default Menu.
  • Branch-specific: select Restaurant and Branch on the menu. Only one enabled branch-wide menu can apply to that pair.
  • Floor-specific: enable Floor-wise Menu and add the floors it serves. Any chosen Company, Restaurant or Branch must match those floors. A floor cannot have two competing enabled floor menus.

For dine-in the application prefers the floor menu, then the branch-wide menu, then Restaurant default. If no menu applies, the profile's permitted Item Groups can be the fallback. Configure an explicit menu when the list must be restricted.

Selecting the table first is therefore important: it determines which floor's menu applies. A takeaway visit has no table/floor and uses the applicable non-floor menu.

[Screenshot: Restaurant Menu showing Restaurant, Branch, Floor-wise Menu, floor assignments and Items with Section/Course and Available]

Set service-specific prices or charges

A service type may have its own selling Price List and Sales Taxes and Charges Template. The list must be enabled, selling and in the profile currency; the tax template must belong to the profile Company.

Only items priced in that service's list are offered for that service. Use this when takeaway prices differ or dine-in has a configured service charge. Leaving the service overrides empty uses the normal pricing/tax defaults.

Test a real cart after configuration. A delivery amount is not automatically created merely because the service is named Delivery.

Configure modifiers and add-ons on Item

Use the Item's Restaurant tab, not repeated menu assignments:

  • Modifier Groups are reusable choices, such as preparation preference. Configure the choices and minimum/maximum selections on Restaurant Modifier Group.
  • An optional choice can have no charge. A chargeable modifier can link an Add-on Item.
  • Optional Add-ons link real sales Items with a quantity/UOM per main selling unit. Their price/tax comes from the transaction's selling setup.

For example, an omelette can offer required egg preparation plus optional cheese. Add-ons are separate priced order lines linked to the main item; they are not a hidden rate adjustment.

Variants inherit the template's restaurant options unless configured on the variant or Override Template Restaurant Options is enabled. An explicit override with empty tables can intentionally suppress inherited choices.

Keep a simple note for an exceptional request, but do not use notes instead of required priced choices. Changes to the master later do not rewrite the choice snapshot of a placed round.

[Screenshot: Item Restaurant tab with one required modifier group and priced add-ons]

[Video: Selecting a variant, completing required choices and adding a priced extra to an order]

pages.title: Arrange Floors and Tables
pages.html:
Use the floor plan to identify where dine-in guests are seated and to open the correct visit.

Build the plan

A manager needs a restaurant-mode profile with the correct Restaurant/Branch. Open Floor, then Floor Editor.

Create the floors, add tables with their labels/seats and arrange their size, shape and position. Add visual elements where useful. Save the plan before staff begin service. Desk forms are another maintenance route for the same floor/table records.

Each floor belongs to one Restaurant/Branch. Tables inherit that location. The same table number can be used on different floors: Main Hall table 1 and Terrace table 1 are not the same table.

New tables are numbered independently on each floor: the first table on a new
floor is T1, followed by T2 and so on. Duplicating a table also uses that floor's
sequence. Existing labels are not renumbered automatically.

Backgrounds and decorative elements help orientation; they do not create service zones, bookings or additional stock locations.

[Video: Creating Main Hall and Terrace, arranging tables and saving the floor plan]

Use the floor during service

Select the relevant floor. Free and Occupied describe the current table occupancy. Occupied tables can show visit time, waiter and guest information; do not read the table colour as a promise of kitchen readiness.

Select a free table to start a dine-in visit. Select an occupied table to open its existing visit rather than starting another party on it. The kitchen's Sent/Preparing/Ready statuses are separate from Free/Occupied.

Move or join tables

To move a party, open its visit and select Transfer table. Choose a free
destination, then select Confirm transfer. The new selection replaces the old
one automatically; confirming releases all previous tables assigned to that visit.
Closing the picker without confirming leaves the current assignment unchanged.

To give the party extra tables, use Join tables, select the extra free tables,
then select Update tables. Do not use Transfer table when you want to keep the
current tables. Tables must belong to the same Restaurant/Branch; joined tables
must have compatible menus and eligible kitchen stations.

Joining tables means one visit and one bill. It is not merging two already occupied visits. Cross-floor joining can be rejected when the floors use different menus or kitchen scopes.

When moving an existing visit, only future rounds use the new routing context. Previously placed rounds retain their original kitchen tickets and production history.

Release a table

Successful billing releases the visit's tables. For an empty visit, use Close session and release tables when offered. A visit with placed rounds needs order cancellation or settlement first; do not just clear its table from the floor plan.

If a table seems occupied incorrectly, inspect the linked visit and use Bill, Cancel and Release Tables. Do not delete its table record to free it.

Guest count is a party count. Individual guest movement, seat assignments and seat-level bills are not tracked.

[Screenshot: Floor showing a free table and an occupied table with waiter and elapsed time]

pages.title: Configure Kitchen Preparation
pages.html:
Use kitchen routing for items that must be prepared after an order is placed. A ready-to-sell bottled drink can remain direct-sale stock; a prepared dish needs a recipe and production setup.

Decide which items need preparation

Kitchen Stations claim ERPNext Item Groups, including descendants. If an item's group matches an eligible station, it is treated as a prepared/QSR item. The catalogue identifies preparation items with a QSR label.

An item not mapped to a kitchen can remain a direct-sale item. Do not map the entire item tree to a kitchen unless every matching sale item should need production.

Menu Sections/Courses organize the menu; they do not route preparation.

Prepare the recipe and stock

Enable Stock Reservation in Stock Settings before placing stock-bearing
restaurant orders. This protects promised ingredients/output from being sold to
another order while preparation is in progress.

For each routed main item:

  1. Configure it as a stock Item.
  2. Create an active, submitted default ERPNext BOM for the profile Company.
  3. Use valid ingredient UOMs and quantities.
  4. Put ingredients in the station's raw-material warehouse.
  5. Confirm finished goods will be sold from the POS Profile warehouse.

Optional work-in-progress configuration supports the required transfer/manufacture steps. Standard ERPNext tracking, quality-inspection, manufacturing and whole-number UOM rules still apply.

An ingredient quantity of 0.4 Nos is invalid when Nos must be whole. Fix the recipe or ingredient UOM; do not turn off stock validation to make the menu orderable.

Create the stations

In Kitchen Station, select its name, Company, Restaurant and Branch. Add the Item Groups it prepares and its preparation warehouses.

Use narrower groups for a specialist station. If Tea is mapped to one station and its Coffee child group to another, the closest matching child mapping wins. Two enabled shared stations cannot both claim the same exact group in one Restaurant/Branch.

Route by floor when needed

Leave Floor-wise Station off for a shared station, including takeaway. Enable it and select one or more matching floors for a local kitchen.

For the same Item Group, a matching floor-specific station takes priority over the shared station. Disjoint floor stations may reuse a group. Overlapping floor stations cannot compete for the same exact group.

Example: Main Kitchen is shared for Prepared Food, while Terrace Kitchen handles that same group on Terrace. Takeaway uses the shared station.

Group specificity is resolved before the floor-specific tie-break. A more-specific shared Coffee mapping can therefore beat a floor station mapped only to a broader Drinks group.

[Diagram: Table floor + most-specific Item Group → eligible floor station or shared fallback → ingredient warehouse → finished-goods warehouse]

What placement does

The POS checks recipe ingredients when the prepared item is ordered. Placing the round creates station KOTs, native Work Orders and stock reservations. Preparation manufactures the output; invoicing consumes the sold stock.

An item configured for preparation only on another floor does not silently become a direct-sale item. Fix its routing or choose a permitted temporary station when the prompt offers one. A hidden preferred station is not bypassed by falling back to a visible shared station.

Add-ons follow their prepared parent's routing. Review their stock setup too: a priced extra is still a real Item.

Test before opening

Place one dish from each mapped group, check its KDS destination and complete production. Repeat for each floor and for takeaway. Test an ingredient shortage and confirm staff receive a useful error before placing the order.

[Screenshot: Floor-wise Kitchen Station with Item Groups, selected Terrace floor and raw-material warehouse]

pages.title: Take Dine-in and Takeaway Orders
pages.html:
Use Place Order to commit the next round for the kitchen. It does not collect payment or replace the cashier's bill.

Before service

Sign in as an assigned waiter/service user and open your own shift. Confirm the Restaurant/Branch profile. Choose the service type above the customer. The Restaurant's list for that Branch determines the choices; branches without their own list use the shared, blank-Branch rows.

Dine-in

  1. Choose Dine In or the configured table-required service.
  2. Select the floor and table from the floor plan. You must choose a table before adding items.
  3. Confirm the customer and guest count where needed.
  4. Browse the menu sections, select items/variants, complete required choices and add notes.
  5. Review selling UOM, quantities, add-ons and the calculated totals.
  6. Select Place Order.

The selected floor determines any floor-specific menu and kitchen routing. Closing the table picker does not allow adding dine-in items without a table.

For prepared items, ingredient checks can prevent adding/placing a quantity that cannot be made. A valid price alone does not mean the recipe has stock.

Add another round

Open the same visit from the occupied table or Open Orders. Add new items from the selling catalogue and place the next round.

Items not yet placed can be changed or removed in the cart. Already placed rounds are saved commitments; increasing their quantity in a detail view is not a substitute for a new round. Use the cancellation procedure for an incorrect placed round.

The bill later combines the visit's eligible unbilled rounds. Do not open a new visit for every drink round from the same party.

Takeaway

Choose the configured table-free service, such as Takeaway, then confirm the customer, items and choices and select Place Order. No table is required.

A service-specific price list may offer different items or prices. Floor-only kitchens do not handle takeaway unless an eligible shared route exists.

A table-free service named Delivery works as an ordering label, but the module does not add drivers, delivery tracking or aggregator orders. Record only the delivery information your checkout is configured to collect.

Changes after placement

Move guests to another table

Open their visit and select Transfer table. Choose a free destination on the
floor plan, then select Confirm transfer. You do not need to deselect the old
table: confirming releases all the visit's previous tables and assigns the new one.
Closing the picker without confirming leaves the current tables unchanged.

Use Join tables instead when the same party needs extra tables without leaving
its current ones. Select the extra free tables and choose Update tables.
Tables occupied by another visit cannot be joined or used as transfer destinations.
Joined tables must use compatible menu and kitchen arrangements.

[Video: Waiter transfers an open visit to a free table, then joins an extra table for the same party]

After the first round is placed, the visit's customer is locked. Confirm the customer before then. Placed prices/choices remain recorded even if menu prices or master options change later.

Moving tables affects future rounds, not already issued KOTs. Do not place the same round twice after a slow response; look in Open Orders first.

[Video: Waiter opens Dine In, selects a table, adds modifiers, places a round and later adds drinks to the same visit]

[Screenshot: Shared selling screen with Service Type, customer, menu sections and Place Order]

pages.title: Run the Kitchen Display
pages.html:
Use Kitchen or /vunapos/kitchen to see preparation work as it arrives. A chef with only the kitchen role does not need to open a cashier shift.

Open the correct board

Sign in with an assigned kitchen user. Select the relevant station in the kitchen view. The board lists stations/tickets that user permissions allow for the Restaurant/Branch context, not only tickets created by the current chef.

Stations can receive orders from several POS Profiles in that same Restaurant/Branch. Kitchen Station and Branch restrictions may narrow what a chef sees.

Progress a ticket

Status Kitchen action / meaning
Sent A placed round has arrived; a kitchen user can Accept it.
Accepted Kitchen has acknowledged it; Start when preparation begins.
Preparing Work is in progress; Ready completes the required preparation/manufacturing steps.
Ready The items are ready to serve. A service user can mark Serve where appropriate.
Served Service is complete for the ticket; this is not itself proof of payment.
Cancelled Its order was cancelled through the permitted cancellation process.
  1. Open the ticket and check table/service, waiter, items, quantities, notes and modifiers.
  2. Accept it when the kitchen takes responsibility.
  3. Start preparation.
  4. Ready it only after the actual dishes are prepared and the required stock operations can complete.
  5. Service staff use Serve when the items have been handed over.

Only actions permitted by role and current state are shown. A waiter may view progress but is not automatically authorised to accept/start/ready tickets. Chefs do not collect customer payment merely because they can mark food ready.

The board refreshes as work changes. If another terminal already changed a ticket, refresh and use its current state rather than repeating a stale action.

Production errors

Ready is not just a coloured label. It completes the associated preparation workflow and can fail on ingredient availability, tracking, inspection or other ERPNext manufacturing checks.

Read the dish/recipe error, correct the cause through authorised stock/manufacturing staff and retry the same ticket action. A failure is recorded for review; do not create a second order to replace it blindly.

Do not complete a Work Order separately in Desk just to bypass an unclear error without checking its ticket and stock history. If someone already completed production, refresh and review the existing result.

Paper and billing

The KDS does not imply automatic paper printing at kitchen printers. Billing belongs to the cashier's visit workflow. A profile may allow the cashier to finish pending preparation during billing; see Bill, Cancel and Release Tables.

[Screenshot: Station-filtered KDS with tickets in Sent, Preparing and Ready states showing table, waiter and notes]

[Video: Chef accepts, starts and readies a ticket, then waiter marks it served]

pages.title: Bill, Cancel and Release Tables
pages.html:
Use the existing restaurant visit when taking payment. Starting another retail invoice with the same dishes can lose the order links or charge the party twice.

Bill the visit

  1. Sign in as an assigned VunaPOS Cashier and open your own shift.
  2. Open the party's visit from Open Orders or its occupied table. It may have been created by another waiter.
  3. Place intended unsent items, or clear those that should not be ordered, before billing. Review all saved rounds and kitchen progress.
  4. Select View bill, then review the invoice summary and proceed to checkout when ready.
  5. Confirm the shipping address, configured checkout fields, any permitted credit/loyalty information and payment allocations.
  6. Verify integrated payments where used, then complete the sale.
  7. Confirm the resulting invoice/status before issuing the receipt.

The visit is billed as one invoice using Sales Invoice or POS Invoice according to the configured invoice mode. The billing profile must match the visit's Restaurant, Branch, Company and currency.

Successfully settled visits release their tables. Merely opening a bill or payment dialog does not settle the visit or free its tables.

Pending preparation

Normally, complete the kitchen production before billing. If the profile enables Complete Preparation on Billing, an authorised cashier can complete the pending acceptance/transfer/manufacture steps during checkout.

This uses the same native stock checks. It does not mean “ignore ingredient shortages.” Preparation is marked Ready, not Served, and production already completed is not manufactured a second time.

Use the option only when it matches how your team actually operates. For a separate waiter/chef/cashier demonstration, let the chef complete preparation first.

Cancel a mistake before production

Remove an unsent line in the cart before Place Order. For an already placed order, open its available cancellation control, give a reason and obtain manager PIN approval if required.

Kitchen cancellation applies to the order/round and its linked tickets; it is not a free-form delete of one completed dish. It cancels eligible production work and releases the relevant reservations.

If stock has already been transferred/manufactured or the ticket served, the operation can require explicit reversal/correction in ERPNext. Ask the authorised stock/accounts manager. A cancellation prompt is not a waste-recording or refund workflow.

Free an empty table manually

When a visit has no remaining non-cancelled rounds and is eligible, use Close session and release tables. A visit with placed rounds cannot be released just by clearing the cart. Use order cancellation or billing first.

If guests leave without paying, do not press Complete with fictitious Cash. Escalate to the manager's accounting process. This guide does not invent a one-click unpaid-write-off action.

Interrupted billing

Reopen the same visit and inspect its saved bill/payment state before trying again. A visit in Settling may have a bill already linked; recover that result rather than raising another invoice.

See Connection and Submission Recovery and M-Pesa Integration.

[Video: Cashier bills a waiter's two-round visit, confirms payment and checks that the tables become free]

pages.title: Restaurant Troubleshooting

headings.title: A waiter enters without an opening shift, or cannot open one
Menu is empty or an item is missing
QSR item requires a BOM, or has no ingredient stock
Chef cannot see a waiter's ticket
Cannot edit a placed item or change the customer

pages.html:
Use the visit, order and ticket references when reporting a problem. Do not create replacement orders until you know what was saved.

A waiter enters without an opening shift, or cannot open one

Check the signed-in user and role combination, selected profile and that user's own opening session. Only a positively kitchen-only user bypasses the selling shift. An Administrator's shift does not cover another user.

Set Up a Restaurant

Dine-in items cannot be added

Choose the table first. The table determines menu/floor context. Confirm the floor/table is active and belongs to the profile's Restaurant/Branch.

Menu is empty or an item is missing

Check enabled menu/section, item Available, permitted sales item/variant, applicable branch/floor/default menu and service-type selling prices. A service list without that item's price can exclude it.

Build Menus and Item Choices

QSR item requires a BOM, or has no ingredient stock

Check it is a stock item with an active submitted default BOM for the Company. Verify raw materials at the selected station, not just finished goods in the profile warehouse. Correct fractional whole-number UOM quantities in the recipe.

If placement asks for Stock Reservation, enable it in Stock Settings before
retrying the order; an ordinary retail Sales Order's stock exemption does not
apply to this preparation promise.

Configure Kitchen Preparation

No station can be chosen

Check Item Group hierarchy, enabled stations, Restaurant/Branch/floor scope and the user's station permissions. Takeaway needs an eligible shared route. A station on another floor does not automatically cover this one.

Use a temporary selection only among permitted eligible stations; correct the master mapping afterward.

Chef cannot see a waiter's ticket

Confirm the order was actually placed, then check board station filter, current ticket status/history, profile assignment and Branch/Station permissions. An unsent cart has no kitchen ticket.

Mark Ready fails

Read the error for the dish/recipe or native stock/manufacturing restriction. Correct the cause and retry the same action. Do not alter the status directly or recreate the order.

Cannot join/move tables

The table may belong to another visit, or chosen floors may use incompatible menus or kitchen scopes. Use free tables from the same Restaurant/Branch with compatible setup.

Cannot edit a placed item or change the customer

Placed rounds are commitments. Add a new round for more food; cancel an eligible incorrect round through the supported process. The visit customer locks after placement.

Cashier cannot bill

Check cashier role, own open shift, correct profile/location/currency, unsent items, required fields and preparation status. Complete preparation, or use the permitted Complete Preparation on Billing option.

Table stays occupied

Opening checkout is not settlement. Inspect the visit's saved bill/status. For an eligible empty visit, use Close session and release tables; otherwise cancel or settle its rounds first.

Bill, Cancel and Release Tables

What is not configured here

A course label does not schedule firing. A Delivery service does not dispatch a driver. Table seats are not per-guest bills. Kitchen display does not imply kitchen-printer routing. Do not troubleshoot these as missing checkboxes—the workflows are not provided by this module.

pages.title: Checkout Fields and Approval Workflows
pages.html:
Use these settings when the cashier must collect extra information or when a transaction needs approval before submission.

Capture information at checkout

Configure Checkout Fields in POS Settings for shared defaults, or Checkout Field Overrides in an individual POS Profile.

  1. Choose the target transaction: Sales Invoice, POS Invoice or Sales Order.
  2. Select an existing editable field on that transaction.
  3. Set the label, required flag and display order needed by staff.
  4. Enable the row and save.
  5. Open the matching checkout type and test it as the intended user.

Profile rows can stand alone; a field does not first need to be listed globally. For a matching global field, a profile row can change its label, order or required setting, or disable it at that counter. The same transaction/field pair cannot appear twice.

Choose the target transaction carefully: a Sales Order field is not automatically an invoice field. Select choices come from the underlying field's options; define one choice per line there. Read-only fields and layout controls cannot be used as editable checkout inputs.

Saving the configuration does not grant users new Link-record permissions. Required information must be completed before checkout can finish.

Apply an approval process

Create and activate the ERPNext Workflow first. In the profile's Workflow Configuration, enable it for the relevant transaction type.

Checkout saves the transaction in its initial workflow state instead of silently sending it to the next approval step. Find the saved document in the relevant draft view, open it and select an available workflow action when you intend to advance it.

Actions depend on the active workflow, current state, conditions and your roles. If another user must approve, hand the document over rather than submitting a replacement transaction.

When no workflow is active for that type, VunaPOS shows the normal document status rather than trusting an old stored workflow-state value. Disabling a workflow does not itself cancel or approve transactions.

Test before rollout

Test one ordinary cashier and one approver. Verify the requested field is stored on the right document and that the cashier cannot skip approval. Confirm how your business handles any payment taken before final approval.

[Screenshot: A profile-only checkout field and the resulting required input in Sales Order checkout]

[Video: Saving an invoice in its initial approval state and deliberately selecting the next permitted workflow action]

pages.title: Staff Access and PIN Controls
pages.html:
Assign each person their own user account and the POS Profiles they need. A profile controls counter options; roles and record permissions control access to the underlying business records.

Assign the right counter

Add users under the POS Profile's user assignments. Mark the intended default where appropriate. Users with several profiles should check the selected counter when opening a shift.

Use ERPNext roles to grant the required sale, customer, payment and return permissions. Turning on a profile option alone does not grant a missing permission.

For restaurant role assignments, see Set Up a Restaurant. A kitchen-only user is not a cashier, and one user's shift does not cover a colleague.

Restrict visible records

Use standard ERPNext permissions and sharing for customers and addresses. Branch and Kitchen Station User Permissions can narrow restaurant operations. Branch permissions are optional; absence of a Branch restriction is not the same as denying every branch.

Do not describe sharing one address as granting access to all addresses belonging to that customer. The address picker offers only linked addresses that the user is allowed to read.

Use salesperson PINs

When Require Salesperson PIN is enabled, configure enabled people and their PIN roles in Salespeople and Managers. A salesperson PIN unlocks the selling session; it does not replace logging in as an ERPNext user.

Require PIN Before Every Sale locks again after a completed sale. Failed attempts can cause a temporary lockout using the profile's attempt and duration settings. Session expiry may require verification again before checkout.

Use Lock or the available lock control when handing the terminal to another salesperson.

Ask for manager approval

Require Manager PIN to Remove Items controls restricted cart-item removal. Restaurant Require Manager PIN to Cancel Orders is a separate control; it must not be confused with removing an unsent item.

Ask an authorised manager to verify their PIN when requested. Do not share manager PINs as a workaround for normal permission errors.

If access is denied

Confirm the signed-in user, selected profile and current document status first. Ask an administrator to review roles, assignments, Branch/Station restrictions and any active workflow. Do not solve a single missing permission by granting every user System Manager.

[Screenshot: POS Profile user assignments and separate salesperson/manager PIN controls]

pages.title: Connection and Submission Recovery

headings.title: Connection loss is not offline checkout
If checkout was sent but the result is unclear

pages.html:
Use this guide when the terminal disconnects, a payment stays pending or checkout returns an unclear result.

Connection loss is not offline checkout

The terminal caches catalogue information to reduce loading and may still show items after a connection problem. That is not permission to complete financial transactions offline. Checkout, payments and restaurant order placement need the server.

Reconnect and sign in again if your session expired. If the server returns a login/error page instead of a normal response, do not treat that as a successful sale.

Before refreshing, hold any unfinished retail invoice or place the intended restaurant order while online. Mobile pull-to-refresh reloads the browser and clears unsaved cart work; it is not just a harmless price refresh.

If checkout was sent but the result is unclear

  1. Do not take payment or create the same sale again.
  2. Check Sales History, the saved draft or the Checkout queue, as appropriate.
  3. For an integrated payment, check the existing provider transaction.
  4. Record the invoice/order/payment references and ask a supervisor to review an unresolved result.

Closing a dialog is not a refund. A provider-paid transaction can need reconciliation even when the invoice did not finish.

Background invoice submission

When the profile's Enable Background Invoice Submission is enabled, eligible Sales Invoice sales can be accepted with stock reserved while submission finishes afterward. This requires stock reservation; when the required setup is absent, the application uses direct submission instead.

A queued message is not the same as a submitted invoice. Open Sales History → Checkout Queue to review reserved sales needing processing or operator review:

State What to do
Queued Wait for the accepted sale to be processed; do not recreate it.
Processing Allow the current attempt to finish.
Failed Read the error, correct its cause and use the available retry action if appropriate.
Requires Review Ask an authorised supervisor to inspect the document and reservation/payment result before retrying.

Background submission is not a separate offline-sales system and is not a promise that Sales Orders, POS Invoices and restaurant bills all use this same route.

Retry safely

Fix the actual cause: unavailable stock, missing account, invalid tracked stock or approval restrictions. Use the saved transaction's retry action rather than rebuilding a new cart with another payment.

Unresolved submissions can prevent Close Shift. Once the invoice is submitted, confirm the final status in Sales History.

[Screenshot: Checkout queue showing a failed reserved sale, its error text and Retry action]

pages.title: Common Problems

headings.title: No POS Profile or unable to open a shift
Item is missing or has a zero/unexpected price
Insufficient stock even though pieces exist
Checkout requires a field or approval
Paid transaction still appears unpaid or submission is unclear

pages.html:
Start with the symptom below, then use the linked guide. Keep the transaction reference and exact error when asking for help.

No POS Profile or unable to open a shift

Confirm the user is assigned to an enabled profile with an enabled Selling price list in the correct currency. Check payment accounts and whether that same user already has an open shift.

Open and Close Your Shift

Item is missing or has a zero/unexpected price

Check that it is enabled for sales, allowed by the profile/menu and priced for the selected list and UOM. Check the customer and quantity before changing the rate. Non-stock items may need Allow Service Items.

Find Items and Choose Units · Prices and Discounts

Insufficient stock even though pieces exist

Confirm the warehouse and conversion factor. One carton can require many stock pieces. Quantities across different UOM rows share the same stock.

Batch and Serial Allocation

Address is not offered

Check the selected customer, address link and the user's read/share permissions. Do not attach an unrelated customer's address.

Customers and Shipping Addresses

Checkout requires a field or approval

Complete the requested field for the current transaction type, or use the permitted workflow action. A disabled/hidden action may reflect the document state, not a network fault.

Checkout Fields and Approval Workflows

Paid transaction still appears unpaid or submission is unclear

Check whether the invoice/payment was actually submitted and allocated. A sent STK prompt is not payment confirmation. Do not collect money twice.

M-Pesa Integration · Connection and Submission Recovery

Return action is unavailable

Confirm profile permission, original invoice type/profile, submission status and remaining returnable quantity.

Return Items

Looking for a report

Use Sales History for transaction follow-up, Payments for receipts/allocation history and Close Shift for counter reconciliation. Use the appropriate ERPNext accounting/stock reports for formal ledgers; these guides do not imply a separate restaurant analytics suite.

Restaurant-specific problems

For missing menus, unavailable tables, ingredients, kitchen tickets or blocked bills, use Restaurant Troubleshooting.

pages.title: Introduction
pages.html:
View French Documentation

Introduction

CSF OHADA is a collection of ERPNext customizations, regional settings, and compliance features designed for OHADA (Organisation pour l'Harmonisation en Afrique du Droit des Affaires).

It loads SYSCOHADA charts of accounts, imports Account Categories that match common statement lines, and adds reusable templates so the same approved layout can be run every period from live General Ledger data.

What is included

Included Purpose
SYSCOHADA charts of accounts Company setup
Account Categories Filters that work across companies
Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow templates Statement layouts, ready to run
OHADA Financial Report Template Edit those templates or add custom statements

Reports included with the app

The following report templates ship with the app.

Report Description
Profit and Loss Income statement showing revenue, expenses, and net profit for a period.
Balance Sheet Statement of financial position with assets, liabilities, and equity.
Cash Flow Statement of cash inflows and outflows.

You can adapt these templates or define custom statements beyond them. Templates are configured once and reused. There is no need to rebuild reports in Excel each period.

Other reports

Report What it shows
Fixed Asset Register Enhanced Asset listing with revaluation in asset value, depreciation rates per category, and chart-of-accounts numbers when grouped by asset category.

Installation

Frappe Cloud

Don`t have a frappe site? New to ERPNext? Not an expert with cloud management? We've got you covered.

Simply signup with Frappe Cloud for a free trial and create a new site.
Select Frappe Version-16 or above and select ERPNext and OHADA ERPNext Localization from Apps to Install.
You can get started in a few minutes with a new site and a fresh install to try out the simple and cool features of the App.

Manual

Install this app using the bench CLI:

cd $PATH_TO_YOUR_BENCH
bench get-app $URL_OF_THIS_REPO --branch develop
bench install-app csf_ohada
  • Create the company in an OHADA country and choose Syscohada - Plan Comptable avec code.
  • Confirm Account Categories were imported (they are inserted on migrate).

pages.title: Chart of Accounts

headings.title: SYSCOHADA does not appear in Chart of Accounts
Can I keep ERPNext Standard for an OHADA company?

pages.html:
Member countries

OHADA includes 17 Member States located primarily in West and Central Africa:
Benin (BJ), Burkina Faso (BF), Cameroon (CM), Central African Republic (CF), Chad (TD), Comoros (KM), Côte d'Ivoire (CI), Democratic Republic of the Congo (CD), Equatorial Guinea (GQ), Gabon (GA), Guinea (GN), Guinea-Bissau (GW), Mali (ML), Niger (NE), Republic of the Congo (CG), Senegal (SN), Togo (TG).

Chart of Accounts

For the above member countries, Syscohada - Plan Comptable and Syscohada - Plan Comptable avec code will be available on Chart of Accounts options on top ERPNext's Standard options.

The chart is the foundation for every template filter and account numbers on the enhanced asset register.
Account categories are unique across all entities; therefore, the template is reusable and the financial statements are uniform.

Choose a SYSCOHADA chart

Chart Account Number Account Category
Syscohada - Plan Comptable Codes sit in the account name (1011-Capital souscrit, non appelé) Not assigned
Syscohada - Plan Comptable avec code Dedicated number (6-digit posting accounts) Assigned

Standard and Standard with Numbers remain in the list. Charts for non-OHADA countries are still bundled so company setup outside OHADA continues to work.

After the chart exists

  • When adding new child accounts, give them the same Account Category as their parent if they should hit the same statement line.
  • Prefer account category, account_type, and root_type in templates rather than company-specific account names if you decide to edit the templates.

Troubleshooting

SYSCOHADA does not appear in Chart of Accounts

Confirm the company's Country is one of the member states above and that CSF OHADA is installed.

Category-based template lines are empty

The company was likely created with Plan Comptable (no codes). Assign Account Category on posting accounts, or create a new company with Plan Comptable avec code.

Frequently asked questions

Can I keep ERPNext Standard for an OHADA company?

Yes. SYSCOHADA is optional. Category-based OHADA templates will not match Standard account names unless you map categories yourself.

pages.title: Account Categories

headings.title: A line is zero although the trial balance has a balance
Can one template work across companies?
Must I use the imported names?

pages.html:
Account Categories

Account Category groups accounts independent of the company-specific account name. For example, accounts 411 to 418 have the category "Clients" to correspond to the BI - Clients line item on the Balance sheet Asset, instead of listing every account.

CSF OHADA imports a catalogue oriented on the OHADA financial statements on migrate. These categories are assigned to accounts created using Syscohada - Plan Comptable avec code. Moreover, the existing categories continue to be available.

Before you begin

  • Ensure Chart of Accounts is setup.
  • Open a sample posting account and confirm Account Category is set.
  • You can add a new Account Category and update the accounts accordingly.

Use categories in a template

On an Account Data row, filter Account Category you need, for example Clients or Ventes de marchandises. Prefer exact names from the catalogue. Avoid company-specific account names if the same template must run for more than one company.

If you add a child account later, give it the same category as its parent so the template picks it up without need to edit the template.

Troubleshooting

A line is zero although the trial balance has a balance

The posting account has no category, or the category name does not match the row filter. Use View Account Coverage on the template.

Categories are missing after install

Run migrate. The catalogue is inserted then; names that already exist are left unchanged.

Frequently asked questions

Can one template work across companies?

Yes, when every company maps the same categories consistently. Test the output per company.

Must I use the imported names?

Filters must match the Account Category value on the account. Renaming a category without updating templates will drop those lines.

pages.title: OHADA Financial Report Template

headings.title: View a template in the report
A formula references an unknown line
An account is missing from the report
Should I edit a built-in template?
Should I edit a template that is already in use?
Can one template work across companies?
Can a template replace statutory review?

pages.html:
OHADA Financial Report Template

A OHADA Financial Report Template is a reusable blueprint that turns the same submitted accounting data into different presentations. You can standardise headings, reuse calculations, hide zero or supporting rows, control signs and charts, and produce the same approved structure every period without changing the Chart of Accounts.

A template controls grouping, labels, calculations, and layout. It does not by itself make the books compliant with OHADA rules. Recognition, valuation, depreciation, tax, and disclosure must still be configured and professionally reviewed.

This builder extends ERPNext's Financial Report Template.

Before you begin

  • Review the Chart of Accounts and assign Account Categories where the template will filter by category.
  • Decide the report's required lines, calculations, hierarchy, and sign presentation.
  • Choose stable Line References that formulas can reuse.
  • Test the template on a non-production company and period before relying on it for reporting.

Start from a template

Open OHADA Financial Report Template from the Ohada workspace. The app includes Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow templates. Review and adapt those, or create a new template for a controlled reporting requirement.

Create the template

  1. Enter a descriptive Template Name and select the Report Type.
  2. Add rows to the Report Line Items table in the order they should appear.
  3. Select the Data Source for each row.
  4. Give calculated or account data rows a unique Line Reference.
  5. Optionally add Value Columns (for example gross value, depreciation, net value). Leave the table empty for one amount column per period.
  6. Configure formatting, visibility, sign, and chart options.
  7. Save, click View Report, and reconcile the output with standard financial statements.

Choose a row data source

Data source Use it for Example
Account Data Balances selected through account filters or categories All accounts in Ventes de marchandises
Calculated Amount Arithmetic based on referenced rows (and column codes) REVENUE - COST_OF_GOODS_SOLD
Custom API Approved server-side logic unavailable through standard filters A specialised regulatory or management metric
Visual Row Headers, blank lines, or layout structure Operating expenses

Important row fields

Field Meaning
Display Name The line label shown to report readers.
Line Reference A unique code used by calculations. Start with a letter; use letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens.
Show Line Reference When unchecked, the code is hidden on the report but still usable in formulas.
Indent Level Visual indent on the display name (0 heading, 1 subtotal, and so on).
Formula or Account Filter The filter, expression, or API path for the selected data source.
Balance Type Opening balance, closing balance, period movement, debits, or credits. Required for Account Data.
Balance Filter All, or restrict to debit/credit accounts or a net debit/credit line. Pair with Hide If Zero.
Reverse Sign Changes presentation when a line should appear with the opposite sign.
Hide If Zero Removes an empty line from the rendered report.
Hidden Line Keeps a supporting calculation available without displaying it.
Include in Charts Makes the line eligible for the report chart.
Bold Text / Italic Text / Color / Value Type Presentation of the line.

For Account Data, use the filter builder (Account Category, Account Type, Root Type). Turn on Advanced Filtering only for nested and / or JSON.

If the template has Value Columns, open the row and use Value Column Settings only when that measure should differ from the row default.

Build calculations safely

One can define REVENUE and COGS as Account Data rows, then calculate GROSS_PROFIT with REVENUE - COGS. A margin row can use (GROSS_PROFIT / REVENUE) * 100 if REVENUE != 0 else 0 to avoid division by zero.

Allowed functions include abs, round, min, max, sum, sqrt, pow, ceil, and floor. Parentheses must be balanced. A Line Reference must not collide with a Value Column code.

On the bilan, two rows can share the same account filter with Balance Filter Debit Accounts and Credit Accounts, and Hide If Zero, so a third-party(customer/supplier) balance appears on only one side.

Validate coverage and output

Save runs validation. Errors block save (unknown Line References, circular formulas, missing filters, invalid Custom API path).

Click View Account Coverage and pick a company. Missing Accounts shows posting accounts that no Account Data line selects. Filtered Accounts shows what the selected lines include. Check that intended accounts are included once.

View a template in the report

  1. Open OHADA Financial Report Template from the Ohada workspace.
  2. Select a Report Template (Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, or a custom template), Company, and Filter Based On (Fiscal Year or Date Range).
  3. Click View Report on the template.
  4. Set periodicity (Yearly, Quarterly, Monthly, and so on).
  5. Optionally set Account Detail Level, Finance Book, cost center, project, or other accounting dimensions.
  6. Export to Excel if needed; template bold, italic, colour, and currency formats are applied.

Finance can reuse this view for every period and still drill into contributing accounts with Account Detail Level set to Account Breakdown.

Troubleshooting

A formula references an unknown line

Confirm that the source row has a Line Reference and that the formula uses the exact code. Keep references unique and create source rows before dependent calculations.

An account is missing from the report

Review its Account Category and the row's account filter. Also check whether Hide If Zero or Balance Filter suppresses the line.

Frequently asked questions

Should I edit a built-in template?

Use a copy when Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, or Cash Flow must remain available as a baseline. Document every custom calculation and account category dependency.

Should I edit a template that is already in use?

Duplicate it when the original must remain available as a baseline. Disable a template to hide it from the report without deleting it.

Can one template work across companies?

A category-based design can, but each company must map accounts consistently and the output must be tested separately.

Can a template replace statutory review?

The template controls presentation and calculations inside ERPNext. It does not determine whether the report meets local statutory, audit, or filing requirements.

pages.title: Value Columns

headings.title: The net column is wrong on every line
A column heading is missing for last year
Save fails because of a duplicate code

pages.html:
Value Columns

Balance Sheet often needs more than one amount per period on the same line: gross value, depreciations and net value. Rebuilding that grid in a spreadsheet each year is slow and easy to disconnect from the ledger.

Value Columns on OHADA Financial Report Template are named measures that expand across each report period. Leave the table empty to keep one amount column per period, as in ERPNext.

Value Columns change presentation only. They do not change how accounts are posted.

Before you begin

  • Create the OHADA Financial Report Template and its Report Line Items first.
  • Decide which measures you need. Do not add columns only to show several years, periodicity already does that.
  • Choose Column Codes that are unique and not used as Line References e.g GROSS, DEPR, NET.

Add value columns

  1. Open the template and go to Value Columns.
  2. Add a row per measure. Set Column Code and Label.
  3. Set Period Scope if the measure should appear only for the current period or only for previous periods.
  4. Optionally set a Title Template using {label} and {period}. The default is {label} ({period}).
  5. Set defaults that should apply to every line (balance type, or a formula such as GROSS - DEPR).
  6. Save, then override individual lines in Value Column Settings only where a measure must differ.

On the report, measures expand newest period first. For GROSS and NET over 2025 and 2026 the headings are GROSS (2026), GROSS (2025), NET (2026), NET (2025).

Important column fields

Field Meaning
Column Code Code used in formulas and row settings.
Label Base title shown to readers.
Period Scope All Periods, Current Period Only, or Previous Periods Only.
Title Template Optional heading pattern.
Value Type Currency (default), Float, Int, or Percent.
Hidden Compute the measure for formulas but do not print the column.
Empty Column Print the label only. Use as a visual separator.
Default Balance Type Override every Account Data row for this measure. Leave empty to keep each row's Balance Type.
Default is Formula Treat the default as a calculation (for example GROSS - DEPR on every row).
Default Formula / Account Filter Default filter or formula. A line-level setting still wins.

Build calculations safely

In a formula:

  • A Line Reference (TA) is that line in the same measure and period.
  • A Column Code (GROSS) is another measure on the current row and period.

A cycle (NET depends on GROSS and GROSS depends on NET) is rejected on save.

Troubleshooting

The net column is wrong on every line

Check Default is Formula and the default formula on NET. Then check whether a row-level Value Column Setting overrides it.

A column heading is missing for last year

Period Scope may be Current Period Only. Use All Periods unless you intentionally hide prior years.

Save fails because of a duplicate code

Column Code must be unique and must not match any Line Reference.

pages.title: Custom API Rows

headings.title: A calculated row cannot use the result
Can the row call a public REST API directly?
Can the function change accounting data?
What happens when the function raises an error?

pages.html:
Using Custom API Rows

A management-report line may be impossible to produce from account categories alone, for example a specialised budget-adjusted metric calculated by an installed custom app. The value must appear beside standard account lines and remain available to later formulas.

A OHADA Financial Report Template row with Data Source set to Custom API calls an approved server-side Python function. Use it only when Account Data and Calculated Amount rows cannot express the requirement. This is an advanced developer feature, not a way to call an external HTTP endpoint from the report.

Before you begin

  • Use a site where the custom Frappe app can be installed and deployed.
  • Implement and test a module-level Python function in that app.
  • Confirm the function's performance, permissions, data access, and error handling.
  • Create or identify the OHADA Financial Report Template that needs the row.

Add the Custom API row

  1. Open the template.
  2. Add a row in Report Line Items and open its row editor.
  3. Set Data Source to Custom API.
  4. Enter a dotted Python path such as my_app.financial_report_api.get_budget_variance.
  5. Set a Line Reference when later formula rows need the returned value.
  6. Configure Reverse Sign, Hide If Zero, Hidden Line, Include in Charts, and Value Type as required.
  7. Save the template and view report.

Function contract

The method receives the report filters, generated periods, and current row. Return one numeric value for each period, in the same order.

CSF OHADA requires the function to be whitelisted and to permit GET.

from frappe.utils import flt

@frappe.whitelist(methods=["GET"])
def get_budget_variance(filters=None, periods=None, row=None):
    filters = filters or {}
    periods = periods or []
    values = []

    for period in periods:
        variance = calculate_variance(
            company=filters.get("company"),
            from_date=period.from_date,
            to_date=period.to_date,
        )
        values.append(flt(variance))

    return values

Return requirements

Requirement Reason
List of numeric values The report needs one renderable amount per period.
Same length as periods Each displayed period must receive exactly one result.
Same order as periods Values must align with their headings.
Stable Line Reference Later calculated rows use the API result safely.

Important behaviour

The path must use the form app.module.method. The function must exist in an installed app. @frappe.whitelist(methods=["GET"]) is required. Server Scripts are not supported.

The same list is copied to every non-empty Value Column. The function cannot return a different series per measure.

Secure and test the function

Validate filter values, use permission-aware queries, avoid returning sensitive detail, and keep queries bounded. Test no-data periods, multiple periodicities, company separation, and error conditions. Reconcile the result with an independent calculation before publishing the template.

Troubleshooting

The API path is rejected

Use a complete dotted module path. Confirm the function is defined at module level, is whitelisted, and permits GET.

The row shows zeros

Review Error Log for a Custom API error, confirm the function returned one numeric value per period, and test the function with the same report filters.

A calculated row cannot use the result

Give the Custom API row a unique Line Reference and use that exact reference in the later formula.

Frequently asked questions

Can the row call a public REST API directly?

The template calls a Python function on the ERPNext server. That function may integrate with another system according to your app's security design.

Can the function change accounting data?

A reporting function should be read-only. Creating or changing transactions during report execution would make results unsafe.

What happens when the function raises an error?

The app records an error and can fill the row with zeros. Treat that state as a failed calculation and investigate before sharing the output.
