  • at least one Supplier Quotation for the RFQ has been submitted.

The RFQ's Award Status then shows Pending Selection. The status is also refreshed every hour, so RFQs whose deadline passes appear on their own.

Making an Award

  1. On the RFQ, click Award → Award Supplier.
  2. Choose the Award Basis:
  • Full Award: every open item goes to one supplier's quotation.
  • Partial Award: choose the supplier item by item, and leave items open for a later award.
  1. Use Compare Quotations to see each item's bids side by side, cheapest first. The lowest price is marked Lowest.
  2. Pick the winning quotation for each item. Award All on a quotation picks it for every item it covers.
  3. If a pick isn't the lowest price, enter a Justification. It is required.
  4. Save and Submit the award.

The summary at the top shows Items awarded, Suppliers quoted, the Award value and how far the award is Above best prices.

What Submitting Does

  • Marks each item on the RFQ as Awarded and updates the RFQ's Award Status.
  • Sets each supplier's Award Outcome to Awarded or Not Selected, which suppliers see on the portal.
  • Emails the suppliers with the result.
  • If Create Purchase Orders on Award is on in Sourcing Settings, drafts one Purchase Order per winning quotation, with only the items it won.

When that setting is off, open the awarded Supplier Quotation and use Create → Purchase Order. The order includes only the awarded items, and the app refuses Purchase Order lines that weren't awarded to that supplier.

Closing Without an Award

To stop an RFQ without awarding everything, click Award → Close Without Award (or Close Remaining Items after a partial award), and give a reason. The remaining items are marked Not Awarded.

Cancelling an Award

Cancel any Purchase Orders created from the award first, then cancel the award. The items become open again, and suppliers are told the award was withdrawn.

Award Status Reference

Award Status Meaning
Pending Selection Ready for award decisions. No items have been awarded or closed yet.
Partially Awarded Some items have been awarded or closed, while others remain open for a decision.
Awarded All items have been decided, and at least one item has been awarded.
Not Awarded All items have been closed without any awards.

pages.title: 5.1 Confirming Portal Orders
pages.html:
When a customer sends an order from the portal, it arrives as a draft Sales Order with Created from Sourcing Portal ticked.

Finding Portal Orders

  • The Portal Orders to Confirm counter on the Sourcing workspace opens the list of orders waiting for you.
  • In the Sales Order list, filter on Created from Sourcing Portal = Yes and status Draft.

Orders the customer has only saved for later are hidden from staff. You see an order only once the customer has sent it.

Confirming an Order

  1. Open the draft Sales Order.
  2. Check the items, quantities, prices, delivery date and address. Adjust anything that needs it, for example stock availability or taxes.
  3. Submit the Sales Order.

Once it is submitted, the customer sees it as confirmed and can no longer withdraw it. Continue with Delivery Notes and Sales Invoices as usual. The customer follows them on the portal.

Tip

If you need the customer to change the order, contact them before you submit. Until then, they can withdraw it, edit it and send it again.

pages.title: 5.2 Placing Orders
pages.html:
Customers can order from your item catalogue on the portal. Each order arrives in ERPNext as a draft Sales Order for your team to confirm.

Note

Portal ordering is off by default. Turn on Allow Customers to Create Sales Orders in Sourcing Settings → Portal Transactions.

Setting Up Customers to Order

What Where Why
A price list Default Price List on the Customer, its Customer Group, or Selling Settings The portal retrieves prices for every order line from the selected price list. Without one, the customer sees We cannot price orders for your account yet.
Item prices Item Price records for each item and unit customers may order Items without a valid price cannot be ordered. Customer-specific Item Prices take precedence when available.
Companies The Accounts table on the Customer, with one row per company If multiple companies are configured, customers can order only from those listed. This configuration is unnecessary when only one company is used.
Delivery addresses Customer addresses Customers select one of their saved addresses as the delivery address for an order.

Placing an Order (Customers)

  1. Open Sales Order → New order.
  2. Browse or search the catalogue. Filter by item group with the chips at the top, and switch between grid and list views.
  3. Click Add on each item and set the quantity with + and −. The cart on the right shows the lines and the total.
  4. Choose Deliver by, the date you need the order.
  5. Choose Deliver to, one of your addresses.
  6. Optionally enter Your reference, your own PO number.
  7. Click Send order.

Save for later keeps the order as your own draft. Drafts aren't visible to staff until you send them.

Rules

  • The delivery date can't be in the past.
  • A PO number can be used only once per customer.
  • An order can have at most 100 lines.
  • Every item must be orderable and have a price in your price list.

After Sending

  • The order appears under Sales Order with its status.
  • Until staff confirm it, you can withdraw the order. It goes back to your drafts, where you can change it and send it again.
  • Once staff confirm it, it can no longer be changed or withdrawn. Deliveries and invoices then appear under Delivery Note and Sales Invoice.

pages.title: 6.1 Customer Guide
pages.html:
This page is for customers using the portal at https://<your-site>/vuna-sourcing.

Overview

  • Open Quotations, Open Orders, Outstanding and Overdue at the top.
  • Sales Invoices for the last 12 months, and Invoices by Status (paid, unpaid, overdue).
  • Your open quotations and pending deliveries.
  • Account Details: the details the seller holds for you.

Menu

Menu item What you find there
Quotation Quotations sent to you.
Sales Order Your orders. Place new ones using New Order. See Placing Orders.
Delivery Note Deliveries made against your orders.
Sales Invoice Your invoices, including outstanding amounts.
Credit Note Credit notes issued to you.
Credit Note Request Request a credit against an invoice. See Credit Note Requests.
Pending Invoices Outstanding amounts, due dates, and the number of days overdue.

Placing orders and requesting credit notes work only when the seller has turned those features on. Otherwise the page says the feature is turned off.

On a Phone

On a phone, the menu moves to a bar at the bottom of the screen, and lists and documents switch to a single-column layout.

pages.title: 6.2 Supplier Guide
pages.html:
This page is for suppliers using the portal at https://<your-site>/vuna-sourcing.

Overview

The Overview page is the first page you see after signing in.

  • Open RFQs, Open Orders, Outstanding and Paid (12 months) at the top.
  • Purchase Orders for the last 12 months, and Invoices by Status.
  • Your open RFQs and open orders, with links to each one.
  • Account Details: the details the buyer holds for you, such as type, supplier group, currency and tax ID.

Menu

Menu item What you find there
Request for Quotation Requests sent to you. See Quoting on the Portal.
Supplier Quotation Quotations you have drafted or submitted, along with their status.
Purchase Order Orders placed with you, including quantities received so far.
Purchase Invoice Invoices recorded against your orders.
Debit Note Debit notes raised against you.
Pending Invoices Outstanding amounts owed to you, due dates, and the number of days overdue.
Onboard / My Applications Apply for another role or check the status of previous applications.

Printing

Quotations, orders and invoices have a Print button that opens the document in the buyer's print format.

Live Bids

While you are taking part in an open bid, a Live bid panel sits in the corner of every page with the time left and your position. Click it to jump to the bid room. See Open Bids.

Switching Accounts

If your login is linked to more than one supplier, or to a supplier and a customer, use the account menu at the top left to switch between them.

pages.title: 7.1 Trouble Shooting
pages.html:
Onboarding

"We are not taking supplier (or customer) applications at the moment."

The matching Accept … Applications option is off in Sourcing Settings.

The sign-up page asks visitors to request an invitation.

Registration Mode is Invitation Only. Invite the person from Sourcing Settings → Invite Supplier, or switch the mode to Open to Public.

"Your account … was created, but we could not send the setup email."

Outgoing email isn't working. Fix the email account, then send the person a password reset from their User record.

"These supporting documents need attention before this request can be submitted."

A mandatory document is missing, or its expiry date is before its issue date. The message lists which ones.

"{file type} files are not accepted here" / "The file is larger than the … MB limit."

Check Allowed File Types and Maximum File Size in Sourcing Settings, or on the Party Document Type.

"Tax Registration Number … is already on supplier onboarding request …"

Another application or party already uses that number. Check for a duplicate before approving.

RFQs and Bidding

"A sealed bid needs an RFQ Opening Committee to open the quotations."

Choose a committee on the RFQ before saving.

"Set when bids close to a time in the future before submitting."

Bids Close At is empty or already in the past.

"… is a sealed bid. Its quotations can be submitted once the committee opens them."

Wait for the committee to click Open Quotes, then submit the Supplier Quotation.

"Bidding on … is still open."

Open-bid quotations follow the supplier's bids until bidding closes. Wait for the closing time.

"… has not finalised this quotation yet."

The supplier saved a draft on the portal but hasn't sent it.

"Another bidder already holds a bid of …"

In an open bid, two suppliers can't hold the same total. The supplier must place a different price.

"These quotations cannot win."

A chosen quotation has expired (its Valid Till is past), or the supplier is disabled or on hold.

"… is not the lowest total. Explain why it wins in Justification."

Fill in Justification for any winner that isn't the lowest price.

A supplier can't see an RFQ on the portal.

Check that the supplier is on the RFQ's Suppliers table, the RFQ is submitted, and the supplier's Portal Users table includes their login.

Customer Orders

"Ordering on the portal is turned off."

Turn on Allow Customers to Create Sales Orders in Sourcing Settings.

"Your account is not set up for ordering yet."

With more than one company, add the company to the customer's Accounts table.

"We cannot price orders for your account yet."

The customer has no price list. Set one on the customer, its customer group, or in Selling Settings.

"We do not have a price for … yet."

Add an Item Price for that item in the customer's price list.

"You already used PO number … on order …"

Each PO number can be used once per customer.

Credit Note Requests

"Credit note requests on the portal are turned off."

Turn on Allow Customers to Request Credit Notes in Sourcing Settings.

"Invoice … has already been fully credited."

Everything on the invoice has been covered by earlier credit notes.

"Credit note request … is …, so this credit note cannot be submitted."

The linked request isn't Approved. Approve it first, or remove the link.

"Draft credit note … already exists for this request."

Open the existing draft instead of creating another.

pages.title: 1.1 Overview
pages.html:
Vuna Livestock Management System Workspace

Vuna Livestock Is an integrated livestock management app for ERPNext that connects daily farm operations with financial accounting and biological asset valuation, supporting International Accounting Standard 41 (IAS 41)

Who is this solution for?

  • Farm operators recording feed, losses, weights, produce, and observations.
  • Farm managers reviewing flock performance, targets, traceability, and follow-ups.
  • Veterinary and breeding teams maintaining animal-care and reproduction records.
  • Accountants and administrators configuring valuation, permissions, and background processing.

Main capabilities

  • Daily Farm Entry: Record feeding, mortality, weighing, produce, and observations through one responsive Desk screen.
  • Batch and animal management: Manage flock identity, biological dates, capitalization settings, and individual animals through Batches and Serial Nos.
  • Stock movements: Record livestock receipts, transfers, dispatches, and returns using standard ERPNext transactions.
  • Feeding: Maintain feed formulas and record feed issues linked to the flock and house.
  • Mortality: Record animal losses with reasons and review their effect on population and survival.
  • Weighing: Capture average animal weights, sample sizes, measurement times, and recorded weight gains.
  • Produce collection: Record eggs and other farm outputs through linked stock receipts.
  • Veterinary care: Manage diagnoses, treatment plans, withdrawal-period information, and linked medicine issues.
  • Husbandry: Record dated observations, completed farm activities, and structured pregnancy checks.
  • Reproduction: Record breeding services, offspring, newborn stock receipts, and dam/child relationships.
  • Cost capitalisation: Add qualifying feed and treatment costs to existing livestock valuation through linked Repacks.
  • Performance reporting: Review population, survival, weight, feed consumption, interval Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR), and hen-day egg yield.
  • Dashboard summaries: Display Survival Percentage, Feed Consumed, and Internal FCR cards, plus Daily Population and Mortality Trend charts.
  • Age-based targets: Compare actual weight, feed, FCR, and egg yield against submitted daily-age performance profiles.
  • Life-cycle traceability: Follow stock and operational history across related batches, with clearly labelled Repack-inferred relationships.
  • Performance alerts: Detect mortality, below-target weight, and overdue weighing or treatment, with standard ToDos and Notifications for follow-up.

The app supports cost capitalization workflows relevant to biological asset accounting under International Accounting Standard 41 (IAS 41). Read Biological Assets and IAS 41 for the scope of that support.

pages.title: 1.2 How it works
pages.html:
From farm activity to review

  1. Configure Company, accounts, Warehouses, Items, and users in ERPNext.
  2. Receive livestock into a Batch and a livestock house, using submitted stock transactions.
  3. Record feeding, mortality, produce, weighing, and observations. Daily Farm Entry prepares existing document types rather than a separate daily transaction ledger.
  4. Review and submit stock documents through the normal forms and configured approval workflows. Saved Weight Records and completed Livestock Events follow their own document life-cycle.
  5. Review performance and life-cycle reports. Submitted stock records provide quantities; measurements and linked activities supply operational context.
  6. Follow up on enabled performance rules using standard ToDos and Notifications.

Documents and responsibility

Information Authoritative record
Animal inventory and warehouse movements ERPNext stock ledger and batch allocations
Feeding, mortality, and produce Submitted, classified Stock Entries
Average animal weight Scoped Weight Record with explicit weight UOM
Husbandry and observations Livestock Event
Treatment Veterinary Diagnosis and linked stock entries
Biological targets Submitted Livestock Performance Profile assigned to Batch
Follow-up Standard ToDo with managed alert evidence

A Batch's current location does not establish where an old activity occurred. Record Company and historical House on operational records. A missing or inaccessible record can make a comparison unavailable; it must not be interpreted as a zero result.

See Key Concepts and Document Statuses.

pages.title: 1.3 Key Concepts
pages.html:
Term Meaning in this app
Livestock Item ERPNext Item representing a class of animals; batch-based population metrics require count stock UOM Nos or Unit.
Batch / flock A stock-tracked group of animals belonging to one Item.
Serial No Individual-animal identifier used by supported breeding, treatment, and stock workflows.
House An enabled non-group Warehouse used to locate livestock within a Company.
Feed source warehouse Store from which feed is issued; it can differ from the livestock house.
Hatch/Birth Date Verified biological starting date used by performance targets. Age zero is this date.
Performance Profile Submitted daily-age targets; different from a feed recipe.
Feed Formula Feed composition and expected values over a week-based age range.
FCR Feed Conversion Ratio: kg feed divided by kg live-weight gain for an eligible measured interval.
Hen-day yield Eligible egg count divided by daily hen population exposure, expressed as a percentage.
Inferred relationship Batch continuity supported by eligible Repack allocations; not individual-animal ancestry.

The Batch's displayed manufacturing-date age and a Weight Record's legacy Age field are not substitutes for the explicit Hatch/Birth Date used by target comparisons.

For formulas and interpretation, see Calculations and Definitions.

pages.title: 2.1 Requirements and Installation
pages.html:
Software

This repository targets Frappe v16 (>=16.0.0-dev,<17.0.0) and declares Python >=3.14,<3.15. Install compatible ERPNext and HRMS apps on the same site; the app declares both as required dependencies. Use the requirements of the release you actually deploy when maintaining another branch.

A self-hosted installation needs a working Bench environment, database, Redis, workers, and scheduler. This guide begins with an existing Bench and site; it does not describe operating-system installation.

Farm preparation

Before recording transactions, prepare:

  • Company, currency, chart of accounts, and appropriate stock difference accounts.
  • Livestock houses and feed/produce stores as Company Warehouses.
  • Livestock, feed, medicine, and produce Items with verified stock UOMs and conversions.
  • Users, roles, and an active Employee for each Daily Farm Entry operator.
  • Opening stock or receipt documents establishing actual animal and feed inventory.

Prepare verified hatch dates and breeder target tables if using performance profiles. Agree alert thresholds with farm management before enabling rules.

Production Setup

Managed Hosting

You can download the app from Frappe Cloud, a simple, user-friendly and sophisticated open-source platform to host Frappe applications with peace of mind.

It takes care of installation, setup, upgrades, monitoring, maintenance and support of your Frappe deployments. It is a fully featured developer platform with an ability to manage and control multiple Frappe deployments.

Development Setup

Manual Installation

Install compatible ERPNext and HRMS first. From the Bench directory, fetch the repository and install it on your site. Replace all placeholders, including the branch, with your deployment values.

bench get-app https://github.com/navariltd/livestock-management.git
bench --site YOUR_SITE install-app livestock_management

pages.title: 2.2 First Flock Walkthrough
pages.html:
Use a test site and clearly labelled synthetic records. The example uses Navari Demo, livestock Item Demo Layers, Batch DEMO-FLOCK-001, and House A - ND. Do not post demonstration stock into a production farm.

Prepare the flock

  1. Complete Company, Warehouse, Item, and user setup.
  2. Create Demo Layers as a batch-tracked stock Item with stock UOM Nos. Create its Batch and mark Is Livestock Item.
  3. Enter a verified Hatch/Birth Date. For laying-flock comparisons, assign a submitted all-female performance profile with eligible egg Items.
  4. Receive 100 animals into House A using a submitted stock receipt. Receive sufficient feed into the feed store separately.
  5. Check the Batch and warehouse quantities in ERPNext Stock Ledger before entering activities.

Example: Demo Layers batch document

Record

Use a test site and clearly labelled synthetic records. The example uses Navari Demo, livestock Item Demo Layers, Batch DEMO-FLOCK-001, and House A - ND. Do not post demonstration stock into a production farm.

Prepare the flock

two days of activity

  1. Open Daily Farm Entry and select the Company, Item, Batch, House, Employee, and actual activity time.
  2. Record an initial average weight of 1.0 kg using a representative sample of 10 animals.
  3. At a later timestamp, save a feeding entry for 40 kg, then open and submit the resulting Stock Entry.
  4. Record a second average weight of 1.2 kg after the feeding timestamp. Keep population unchanged between the measurements for this FCR example.
  5. For a separate two-day feed/yield comparison, use 100 g/animal/day targets and 160 eligible eggs over two days of 100 closing hens. Submit the produce receipts.

The measured interval gives FCR 40 / (100 × (1.2 − 1.0)) = 2. The separate two-day intake target is 20 kg and hen-day yield is 80%. Feeding 40 kg over that same two-day period would give a +20 kg feed variance; choose the report dates to match the example being checked.

Review

Open Livestock Batch Performance report, select the Company, Item, Batch, House, and relevant dates, and inspect Data Notes. Open Lifecycle Traceability on Batch to check receipts and activities. Refresh the workspace summaries with matching scope and dates; cards may default to the current month rather than the report's last 30 days.

pages.title: 3.1 Company and Accounting
pages.html:
Set up your business as an ERPNext Company with the correct currency, chart of accounts, fiscal periods, and stock accounting configuration. Work with your accountant to choose the ledger accounts used for your farm activities.

Configure livestock settings

  1. Open Company from Desk search and select your Company.
  2. Review the livestock stock entry difference account fields: Feeding, Mortality, Treatment, Egg Production, and Capitalization.
  3. Select appropriate accounts in that Company. Your medical stock issues need the Treatment Stock Entry Difference Account in the same Company and currency. Choose appropriate non-Stock difference accounts.
  4. Find Auto-close Performance ToDos on Recovery, placed in the Lvm Settings tab, and decide whether it should be enabled. The default is off, leaving verified recovered tasks open for manual closure.
  5. Save your Company settings. Review the first posted transaction with your accountant to confirm its stock and ledger effects.

The screenshot below shows demo accounts, consult your accountant/ERPNext consultant for proper account mapping.

Company livestock difference accounts and recovery auto-close setting, using demo account names

The app maps these Company settings to difference accounts on supported Stock Entry rows before saving. Normal ERPNext accounting validations still apply. A setting does not create opening stock, determine farm accounting policy, or approve capitalisation automatically.

pages.title: 3.2 Warehouse and Livestock Houses
pages.html:
Set up each of your livestock houses as an ERPNext Warehouse so you can track animals and activities by their physical location.

  1. Open Warehouse and create an appropriate hierarchy under your Company.
  2. Create each physical livestock house as an enabled non-group Warehouse.
  3. Create separate feed, medicine, and produce stores as needed.
  4. Receive livestock into the actual house and supplies into their stores.
  5. Grant operators access to both the house and any source/destination stores required for their work.

Example: Warehouse tree showing livestock houses

In Daily Farm Entry, House identifies where the animals were located. A feeding row's source warehouse identifies where the feed came from. Selecting the feed store as the House misstates the animal location and can prevent population checks.

Use a submitted Material Transfer when animals change houses. Do not edit Batch Location to replace a physical stock transfer. Reports use historical movements and explicit activity locations, not just the Batch's current location.

pages.title: 3.3 Items and Units
pages.html:
Create separate Items for your animals, feed, medicine, and produce. Choose units that match how you count, issue, and receive them.

Livestock

Create an enabled stock Item with batch tracking for flock workflows. Population, survival, and related-batch inference are designed for whole animals with stock UOM Nos or Unit. Individually identified animals may use serial tracking in supported standard-form workflows; Use standard forms for your serial-tracked animals; Daily Farm Entry supports batch-tracked, non-serialized flocks.

Example: livestock item screenshot showing item details including default UOM

Example: item's Serial Nos/Batches section

Feed and medicine

Use separate stock Items for feed and medicines. For feed reporting, prefer stock UOM Kg or configure a valid Item conversion to Kg. A bag quantity must have a verified mass conversion; the app cannot infer a bag's weight from its name.

Daily Farm Entry accepts quantities in the selected Item's stock UOM. Use the standard Stock Entry form when entering an alternative transaction UOM. Reports read stock quantities, then convert mass once.

Example: feed item with UOM set as Kgs

Eggs and other produce

Use separate Items for produce categories. For hen-day yield, eligible egg Items must use count stock UOM Nos or Unit. Include cracked and damaged categories in the profile when they represent eggs laid. Configure tray/carton transaction conversions to count stock UOMs in ERPNext.

Keep feed, produce, and livestock as different Items. Configure inventory batches for feed or produce when those Items require batch tracking.

pages.title: 3.4 Batch and Serial Numbers
pages.html:
Use a Batch to identify each flock or intake of animals you manage together. Use Serial Nos where you need to identify individual animals.

Batch setup

  1. Create a Batch for the livestock Item using standard ERPNext batch setup or the receipt workflow.
  2. Mark Is Livestock Item for dashboard summaries and performance alerts.
  3. Enter the verified Hatch/Birth Date for biological target comparisons.
  4. Select a submitted Performance Profile when targets are available.
  5. Review Location and capitalization settings where used, then save.

Batch showing Is Livestock Item, Hatch/Birth Date, Performance Profile, and Lifecycle Traceability button.

Creating a Batch does not create livestock stock. Submit a receipt into the actual house. A Batch belongs to an Item; stock movements establish its Company and warehouse quantities.

The target report uses Hatch/Birth Date with no manufacturing-date fallback. If your Batch displays age based on Manufacturing Date, treat that as a separate display; enter Hatch/Birth Date for target comparisons. Reassigning a profile changes historical comparisons; use document history to review assignment changes.

Individually identified livestock

Use ERPNext Serial Nos for supported individual-animal workflows, including dam/sire links and serial-specific veterinary capitalization. Configure serial creation on the Item before receiving animals. Do not assume batch dashboard calculations support every serial-only workflow.

The Batch Life-cycle Traceability button opens the life-cycle report and proposes the user's default Company.

pages.title: 3.5 Feed Formulas
pages.html:
Create a Feed Formula for each feed recipe and age range your farm uses. Keep recipe planning here and use a Performance Profile separately when you want daily-age target comparisons.

  1. Search for Feed Formula using an authorised account.
  2. Enter Formula Name, Age From (Weeks), and Age To (Weeks).
  3. Record Expected Intake and Expected Food Conversion Rate as agreed by the farm team.
  4. Add the feed ingredient rows and save.
  5. Select the formula on supported Stock Entries when relevant and verify the actual issue rows.

Feed Formula with week-based age range, expected values, and ingredient rows.

The formula is a saved, non-submittable record. Its expected fields are not automatically copied into the daily-age target comparison table, and selecting a formula does not prove feed was consumed. Submitted Feeding Material Issues provide recorded consumption.

pages.title: 3.6 Performance Profiles
pages.html:
Create a Livestock Performance Profile for the breed and production stage you manage. Open it from Desk search with a Stock Manager or System Manager account. Enter a descriptive profile name, then add one target row per biological age day or use standard Frappe Data Import with child rows. Age zero is the hatch/birth date. Export a template first to obtain the correct parent and child column names.

Target Unit
Average weight kg per animal
Daily feed intake g per animal per day
Interval FCR kg feed per kg live-weight gain
Hen-day egg yield percentage

Leave an individual target blank when unspecified. Enter 0 for an explicit zero. Use blank cells for targets you do not have; a blank remains different from an explicit zero. Negative, non-finite, and non-numeric targets are rejected. Ages must be unique non-negative whole days; egg yield cannot exceed 100%.

For an all-female laying flock, enable All-Female Laying Flock and select all egg Items laid, including cracked and damaged eggs. These must be stock Items counted in Nos or Unit. Do not select non-egg produce. Hen-day yield is unavailable for mixed-sex flocks or profiles not declared as laying flocks.

Submitted daily-age profile including age zero, optional targets, laying-flock setting, and egg Item categories.

Submit the profile. On each Batch, select its Performance Profile and enter the verified Hatch/Birth Date. Manufacturing date is not used as a fallback. Existing batches are not assigned automatically. Stock Users can read profiles; Stock Managers and System Managers can create, import, submit, cancel, and amend them. To revise targets, amend or create a new submitted profile and reassign the Batch. The current assignment determines historical comparisons; Batch version history records assignment changes.

Batch with verified Hatch/Birth Date and assigned submitted performance profile.

pages.title: 4.1 Receiving Livestock
pages.html:
Record the animals arriving at your farm through ERPNext stock transactions so your house balances and population reports reflect the animals you actually hold.

  1. Prepare the livestock Item, Batch or Serial Nos, Company, and destination house.
  2. For a supplier delivery, create a Purchase Receipt using the standard purchasing workflow. For a suitable non-purchase receipt, use a Material Receipt Stock Entry according to your accounting policy.
  3. Enter the actual posting date/time, livestock Item, whole-animal stock quantity, destination house, and batch/serial allocations.
  4. Review valuation and required accounts, then submit using the normal approval process.
  5. Verify the stock ledger and Batch balance in that house.

Example: Submitted livestock receipt via purchase receipt with posting date, Batch allocation, quantity, and destination house.

Purchase receipt item showing serial and batch no section

For births, use Breeding and Offspring so the linked Offspring Record can support a Birth classification. An unlinked historical receipt remains a Receipt in lifecycle reporting.

pages.title: 4.2 Daily Farm Entry
pages.html:
Use Daily Farm Entry to record your feeding, mortality, weighing, produce, and observations from one screen. You can use it in a desktop or mobile browser while connected to your site. Each activity creates the operational document your team reviews and approves.

Before starting

Use an authorized account with an active Employee in the Company. The enabled livestock Item must be batch-tracked and non-serialized. The selected Batch must have positive available stock in the selected house at the activity time.

Daily Farm Entry context with Company, Batch, House, Employee, and timestamp selected.

Record an activity

  1. Open Daily Farm Entry from the Livestock workspace/sidebar or Desk search.
  2. Select Company, Livestock Item, Batch, House, activity date/time, and Employee. Add Project or Shift where needed.
  3. Choose Feeding, Mortality, Produce, Weighing, or Observation.
  4. Enter the activity details and save that activity.
  5. Open the resulting document to review its values and complete standard submission or workflow steps where applicable.
  6. Review recent activity before recording another event. Each save is independent; saving one activity does not save other unfinished forms.

Feeding activity with stock-UOM quantity and source store.

Activity Result Required follow-up
Feeding Draft Feeding / Material Issue Stock Entry Review and submit
Mortality Draft Mortality / Material Issue Stock Entry Review and submit
Produce Draft Produce Collection / Material Receipt Stock Entry Review valuation and submit
Weighing Saved Weight Record with Kg UOM and explicit scope Review measurement accuracy; no submission step
Observation Saved Open Livestock Event Review and mark Completed when the activity is finished

Saved result with link and status of the created operational document.

Limits

Activity time cannot be in the future or before a recorded Batch manufacturing date. Feed/produce quantities use stock UOM, and produce requires a positive rate. Mortality and weight sample sizes must be positive whole counts within available population. Structured Pregnancy Checks and serial-tracked operations belong in standard forms.

pages.title: 4.3 Feeding
pages.html:
Feeding

Record the feed you issue to each flock using a Feeding / Material Issue Stock Entry linked to its Batch and house. Submit the entry after review so the quantity appears in your consumption summaries.

  1. Ensure feed stock is available in the correct source store and conversions to Kg are configured.
  2. In Daily Farm Entry select the animals' Company, Batch, House, and activity time.
  3. Choose Feeding and add the feed Item, quantity in its stock UOM, source warehouse, and inventory Batch if required.
  4. Save, open the generated Stock Entry, verify the livestock Batch/House header and feed rows, and submit through the normal process.
  5. Refresh Feed Consumed or run the batch report for matching dates.

Submitted Feeding Material Issue showing livestock Batch/House and feed stock quantity/source store.

A draft contributes no posted consumption. The feed's inventory Batch is separate from the header livestock Batch being fed.

A feed store is the issue source; the livestock House is the animal location. Missing historical House can make house-level summaries unavailable. Use the standard form for alternative transaction UOMs and serial-controlled stock.

If the livestock Batch has Active capitalisation and the issue qualifies, submission can also create a Capitalisation Repack.

pages.title: 4.4 Mortality and Culling
pages.html:
Record deaths when they occur, against the affected flock and house. Your submitted mortality issues reduce animal stock and update mortality and survival monitoring.

  1. Create any needed Mortality Reason records with an authorised account.
  2. Open Daily Farm Entry, select the flock context, and choose Mortality.
  3. Enter the reason and a positive whole-animal quantity no greater than available stock in that house at the posting time.
  4. Save, open the generated Mortality / Material Issue, review, and submit.
  5. Check the stock ledger, Mortality Trend, and the performance report for the same scope.

Submitted Mortality issue with reason, animal quantity, Batch, and house.

For 100 animals with 5 deaths and no entrants, closing population is 95 and period survival is 95%, subject to valid stock history.

pages.title: 4.5 Weighing
pages.html:
Use Weight Record to track your flock's average weight over time. Weigh a representative sample and record the average per animal, rather than the total sample or flock weight.

  1. Select the Company, Batch, actual House, and measurement timestamp in Daily Farm Entry.
  2. Choose Weighing and enter a representative whole-number Sample Size plus positive Average Weight in kg/animal.
  3. Save and review the resulting Weight Record. The screen records explicit Company, House, and Kg UOM, plus population at measurement time.
  4. Repeat at a later timestamp using the same scope and a representative sample.

Weight Record with measurement timestamp, Company/House, Kg UOM, sample size, and average weight.

Weight Records are saved, non-submittable records. Their Recorded Weight Gain is Actual Weight minus Previous Weight; Internal Feed Conversion Ratios (FCR) separately validates the historical interval and stock population. For manually entered or older measurements, confirm Company, House, and weight UOM so they can be included reliably.

FCR uses the latest two eligible measurements in the selected period for each active Batch/House. It needs two eligible measurements with different timestamps, positive live-weight gain, and an eligible unchanged population between them. One weight can support a weight-target comparison but cannot establish interval FCR.

pages.title: 4.6 Produce Collection
pages.html:
Record the eggs and other produce you collect from each flock, including their quantities and destination store. Your submitted produce receipts add output stock without increasing animal population.

  1. Configure distinct produce Items and destination stores.
  2. Select the livestock Batch and House in Daily Farm Entry, then choose Produce.
  3. Add produce Item, positive quantity in stock UOM, destination warehouse, required inventory Batch, and positive valuation rate.
  4. Save and review the draft Produce Collection / Material Receipt before submitting.
  5. Review period produce totals and, for eligible laying flocks, hen-day yield in the batch performance report.

Submitted Produce Collection with separate normal and damaged egg Items, stock counts, and destination store.

For hen-day yield, configure all laid egg categories in the assigned all-female profile, including cracked/damaged eggs. Non-egg produce does not count toward that yield.

If entering trays/cartons on the standard Stock Entry form, verify their conversion to count stock UOMs. The report uses stock quantity once; it must not multiply an already-converted count again. Daily Farm Entry itself takes stock-UOM quantities.

Use the batch performance report to review Produce Collection receipts. The separate Produce Report selects Production-type entries, so it may not show those same receipts. See Operational Reports.

pages.title: 4.7 Husbandry and Observations
pages.html:
Use Livestock Event to record the husbandry work and observations your team carries out. First create the Husbandry Practice categories you need, then record who performed each activity and when.

  1. For a simple observation, open Daily Farm Entry and select the flock context.
  2. Choose Observation, select the Husbandry Practice, and enter notes and optional end time.
  3. Save the resulting event. It initially has status Open.
  4. Open the Livestock Event, confirm Starts On, Ends On, Company, House, Batch, and Performed By, then set Completed once the activity has been performed.

Completed Livestock Event with start/end times, practice, performer, and notes.

Completed events are included in lifecycle history. Planned/open work does not represent a completed lifecycle activity. Ends On must not precede Starts On; if omitted, it defaults to Starts On.

Use the standard Livestock Event form for Pregnancy Check, including individual Serial No and structured pregnancy details. Daily Farm Entry intentionally excludes that practice. Completed pregnancy checks participate in reproduction counts; a general free-text observation does not replace them.

pages.title: 4.8 Veterinary Care
pages.html:
Use Veterinary Diagnosis to record your animals' symptoms, diagnosis, treatment plan, course dates, and medicines consumed. Open the diagnosis form separately from Daily Farm Entry.

Record and complete treatment

  1. Open Veterinary Diagnosis with a role authorized to create and submit it.
  2. Select Company and the affected Item, Batch, or Serial No. Enter Diagnosis Date, disease, symptoms, recommendations, Start Date, End Date, and Withdrawal Period where relevant.
  3. Add treatment plans. Enter medicine Quantity Consumed in stock UOM and its Source Warehouse, plus required stock batch/serial allocations. Clinical dose information alone does not issue stock.
  4. Keep unfinished follow-up Pending. Saved Pending diagnoses are drafts and can be detected by overdue-treatment rules.
  5. Review consumed stock and Stock Posting Date. Set Completed and submit once the treatment record is ready.
  6. Review the linked Medical Stock Entry and, when enabled, Capitalization Stock Entry.

Submission creates stock transactions; it is not just a clinical status change. Confirm Company treatment account and medicine availability beforehand. See Treatment Costs for capitalization and invoice allocations.

Diagnosis with Pending status, dates, animal identity, symptoms, and treatment plans.

Completed submitted diagnosis with linked Medical and Capitalization Stock Entries.

Follow-up and cancellation

Overdue Treatment uses a Pending diagnosis's End Date; it does not track whether each dose was administered. For house-specific reporting, record reliable historical location through the supported capitalisation warehouse or linked medicine issue's House.

Use normal cancellation procedures for submitted diagnoses. Their linked entries are cancelled in dependency order, subject to ERPNext checks. Do not assume entering a withdrawal period automatically blocks sales; verify your farm's release controls separately.

pages.title: 4.9 Breeding and Offspring
pages.html:
Record your breeding services and births so you can follow individual dams, sires, and offspring. Prepare your livestock Items, Serial Nos, batch creation settings, Company, and receiving house before starting.

Breeding and pregnancy checks

  1. Create Breeding Record with Dam, Service Date, Breeding Method, Sire or semen details, technician, and relevant notes.
  2. Review and submit. The controller updates the dam's service count; cancellation reverses that count.
  3. Record a structured Pregnancy Check using Livestock Event and the dam's Serial No, then mark it Completed when performed.

Submitting your Breeding Record updates the dam's service count. If you consumed stock during the service, record and verify its inventory issue separately; entering consumption details on this form does not create that stock issue.

Submitted Breeding Record with dam, sire/service method, and service date.

Record births

  1. Create Offspring Record, select Company, Target Warehouse, Date of Birth, Posting Date, dam/sire and Breeding Record where known.
  2. Add a child row for each newborn. Configure its Item and any required Batch or requested Serial No.
  3. Verify automatic batch/serial creation settings when identifiers should be generated.
  4. Submit. The app creates and submits a linked Material Receipt, receiving one animal per offspring row.
  5. Review actual received serials/batches, stock quantities, and the dam's children list. Use Hatch/Birth Date on a reporting Batch when biological comparisons are needed; do not assume it is populated automatically.

Offspring Record child rows and its linked newborn Material Receipt.

A linked readable submitted Offspring Record allows the life-cycle report to identify the receipt as Birth. These links do not convert all inferred batch transformations into genetic genealogy.

pages.title: 4.10 Transfers and Dispatches
pages.html:
Use stock transactions to record your animals' actual movements. Keep the Batch and serial allocations accurate so your house balances and life-cycle history stay consistent.

Move animals between houses

  1. Create a standard Material Transfer Stock Entry for the Company.
  2. Enter source and destination Warehouses, livestock Item, stock quantity, and the actual Batch/serial allocations.
  3. Review posting timestamp and submit.
  4. Confirm departure and arrival in the stock ledger and life-cycle report.

A transfer changes location. It is not a birth, sale, or mortality event. House-filtered population and exposure change when animals enter or leave that house.

Dispatch and return

Use standard ERPNext Delivery Note, or a stock-updating Sales Invoice where appropriate, to record physical customer dispatch. Allocate the actual animal Batch/Serial Nos and warehouse. Use the corresponding standard return workflow for customer returns.

Life-cycle sales coverage follows physical stock movements. Non-stock invoices and revenue-only billing do not add dispatch events, and billing linked to a delivery must not be counted as another animal departure.

Batch transformations

Record legitimate splits, merges, or replacements using reviewed Repack transactions with complete stock allocations. The lifecycle report infers continuity only when count and access checks pass. It labels cross-Item replacement as Reclassification / possible grading because stock records alone cannot prove grading intent.

pages.title: 5.1 Workspace Dashboard
pages.html:
Open Vuna Livestock in Desk to access your daily work, reports, and flock summaries. Choose the cards and charts your team needs, and check that users can read the underlying farm records.

Add and review summaries

  1. Confirm a default Company for the user and accessible livestock Batches marked Is Livestock Item.
  2. Check submitted animal/feed stock movements and explicit measurement scope.
  3. If a summary is not already present, use the standard workspace editor with an authorised role to add the installed Number Cards and Dashboard Charts.
  4. Select the intended scope and historical dates where supported, then refresh.
  5. Open the underlying report or documents to investigate a result.

Workspace showing populated cards and charts.

The summaries are operational counts, percentages, mass, or ratios; they should not be read as currency. Available components include Survival Percentage, Feed Consumed, Internal FCR, Daily Population, and Mortality Trend.

Cards generally default to the current month through today, whereas chart timespans and report filters can differ. Align dates and Company before comparing figures. The Daily interval is required for the two historical trend sources.

pages.title: 5.2 Batch Performance Report
pages.html:
Use Livestock Batch Performance report to review each of your flocks in one row. Compare its stock movements, feeding, weight, and produce with the age-based targets you have assigned.

Run the report

  1. Search for the report in Desk or open its Livestock workspace link.
  2. Select required Company, From Date, and To Date. Dates default to the last 30 days through today.
  3. Optionally select Batch and Livestock House / Warehouse. The Batch must belong to the selected Item and House to the selected Company.
  4. Run the report and read Data Notes alongside numeric results.

Report filters and population, feed, and measurement columns for one flock.

Read the hierarchy

Expand or collapse an Item to show its Batches. Each indented Batch keeps its own population, weight, feed, produce, targets, and Data Notes. Item rows are headings only: ratios, percentages, and quantities with different units are not combined into Item totals.

The first Livestock Item / Batch column links headings to Items and child rows to Batches. Items and Batches are sorted by their identifiers. Historical batches do not need the dashboard's Is Livestock Item checkbox to appear in this report.

Read the columns

Group What to review
Identity Batch, Item, population UOM, age at report end, assigned profile
Population Opening, incoming, outgoing, closing, period mortality, period survival
Measurements Latest valid average weight, timestamp, sample size, and measurement age
Consumption and output Period feed in kg, generic produce quantity and its UOM
Interval FCR Actual ratio and start/end measurement dates
Targets Weight/feed/FCR targets, actual-minus-target variances and percentages
Laying performance Configured egg count, actual/target hen-day yield, variance in percentage points

A Batch without a profile can still show available actuals; target columns remain blank. Biological target age needs Hatch/Birth Date. Weight comparison age is the measurement age, not report-end age.

Select a House where a Batch occupies multiple houses; one house's sample does not represent all animals automatically. Multi-house eligible FCR intervals are combined by biomass gain, and notes explain interval differences. Do not assume period feed and interval FCR use identical dates.

pages.title: 5.3 Performance Target Comparisons
pages.html:
Compare your recorded flock results with the targets for its breed and age. First configure and assign a Performance Profile using verified breeder or farm targets.

Open Livestock Batch Performance report and select Company and dates, and optionally Livestock Item, Batch, and House. Leave Livestock Item blank to compare Batches grouped under all accessible eligible Items. Population-based targets require stock UOM Nos or Unit.

  • Weight targets use the age on the latest valid weight measurement, not the report end date. Weight Records need explicit Company, House, Kg UOM, positive average weight and valid sample size. Choose a House when a batch occupies multiple houses; a single-house sample does not represent a multi-house batch.
  • Period feed target is the sum of daily closing population × the matching age's intake in grams ÷ 1,000. Actual feed uses submitted Feeding Material Issues and stock quantities converted to kg.
  • Compare FCR over the measured interval shown in the report, using the same rules as the Number Card: feed between two weights divided by live-weight gain, with no population-changing movements between the measurements. Both measurements must be within the report period. The target is selected at the ending measurement's age. For multiple houses, actual and target FCR are weighted by biomass gain; the data notes list each house's interval and date columns show their overall bounds.
  • Hen-day yield is 100 × configured egg count ÷ the sum of daily closing hen populations. The target is the population-weighted average of daily yield targets. Submitted produce receipts use stock quantity, so trays or cartons already converted to Nos/Unit are not converted again. Non-egg Items are excluded from egg yield but remain part of generic produce totals.

Variance is actual minus target. Percentage variance is unavailable when the target is zero. Egg-yield variance is in percentage points. There is no automatic good/bad coloring.

Daily targets are exact matches with no interpolation. A missing target on any day with positive population leaves the corresponding period target blank. Missing dates, inaccessible records, unknown units or houses, invalid population exposure, and unsupported FCR intervals produce blank comparisons with a note instead of a partial total. An actual value of zero means no matching readable operations were recorded; it does not prove an unrecorded operation never occurred.

Report actuals, targets, signed variances, weight measurement age, and FCR dates.

pages.title: 5.4 Batch Lifecycle Traceability
pages.html:
Use Batch Lifecycle Traceability to follow your flock's receipts, care, stock movements, and dispatches. Open it from your Livestock workspace or Desk search, or select Lifecycle Traceability on your saved Batch. Select Company, Batch, and To Date. From Date, Warehouse, and Event Type are optional; Include Related Batches defaults on.

Use the report to review your history, then open the source document when you need to investigate or correct a record. Running the report does not change your stock or repair missing historical links.

Events and quantities

Event Source
Receipt / supplier return Submitted Purchase Receipts, stock-updating Purchase Invoices and other posted receipts
Birth Material Receipts linked to a readable submitted Offspring Record
Transfer Material Transfers; departures and arrivals appear separately by warehouse
Split / merge / replacement Complete, count-balanced Repack allocations
Reclassification / possible grading Eligible Repack relationships between different Items; grading intent cannot be proven
Capitalisation Capitalisation Repacks, without creating parent/child relationships
Mortality / culling Submitted stock issues using the corresponding entry type
Sale / customer return Delivery Notes and stock-updating Sales Invoices; non-stock billing is excluded
Correction Stock Reconciliation
Feeding / produce collection Submitted header-linked Stock Entries
Treatment Submitted completed Veterinary Diagnoses and submitted linked medicine issues
Husbandry Completed Livestock Events, using Starts On
Weighing Saved, non-cancelled Weight Records, using measurement time

Animal quantities come from stock ledger batch allocations, including legacy batch numbers and Serial and Batch Bundles. A bundle replaces the legacy field; the report never adds both. Allocations are grouped once per document, batch, and warehouse. Incoming and outgoing values remain separate, so same-batch Repacks can show both without representing new animals.

Feed, medicine, produce, weights, and husbandry are linked activities with blank animal quantities. The Activity Warehouse column identifies their explicit historical location. Treatment documents and capitalization entries retain their own rows and readable references to the common diagnosis or stock issue. Summing incoming quantities alone does not calculate a current population: transfers and Repacks can have both sides.

Chronological lifecycle rows with source links, transfers, and activity status.

Chronological lifecycle rows with source links, transfers, and activity status.

Related batches and evidence

Related history is inferred from readable submitted Repack records whose entire stock allocation agrees with the accessible stock ledger. The report requires positive whole-animal quantities in compatible count UOMs, complete batch allocations, and balanced inputs and outputs. Non-livestock, inaccessible, incomplete, or unbalanced allocations prevent inference.

One-to-many splits, many-to-one merges, and one-to-one replacements create relationships labelled Inferred from Repack. Unchanged batch quantities and cost capitalization create no relationships. A partial split can retain some stock under the original batch. An unchanged allocation alongside a transformation is excluded from the relationship.

Eligible split/merge event with parent/child links and Inferred from Repack evidence.

Many-to-many or otherwise ambiguous Repacks appear as Ambiguous transformation, with only readable associated batches listed; they do not expand the lineage. This report cannot establish individual-animal ancestry or resolve ambiguous legacy transactions.

Expansion follows valid relationships in both directions, including connected co-parent and sibling branches. Parent, child, and related batch names link to their Batch forms. Traversal is cycle-safe and limited to 200 batches and 20 relationship levels; exceeding either limit raises an error instead of returning an apparently complete partial history. Disable Include Related Batches to inspect one batch.

Relationship discovery covers all history up to To Date. From Date, Warehouse, and Event Type apply afterward to displayed events, so they do not hide an ancestor needed to reach a related batch. To Date remains the historical cutoff for both discovery and events.

pages.title: 5.5 Operational Reports
pages.html:
Use these reports to investigate your feeding, mortality, produce, inspection, and treatment records. Search by the report name in Desk if your workspace uses a different shortcut label.

Report Intended review Filters to start with
Feeding Feed issues and source transactions Company, date range, optional Stock Entry, Batch, source Warehouse, Item
Mortality Report Classified mortality issues Company, dates, optional Stock Entry and source Warehouse
Produce Report Legacy production entries and grouped output Company, dates, optional Stock Entry, Batch, target Warehouse, Item
Livestock Inspection Report Inspection records Use the report's available inspection and date filters
Livestock Treatment Report Treatment records Use the report's available treatment and date filters

Investigate a result

  1. Choose a Company and a narrow known posting-date range.
  2. Run the report with minimal additional filters.
  3. Open a source document and confirm its type, purpose, Batch link, warehouse, stock quantity, and status.
  4. Compare against the stock ledger and the newer batch performance report as appropriate.

Feeding report with visible scope and linked source issue

Mortality Report for a known submitted loss entry.

Filters and status coverage vary across older reports. Use the lifecycle/performance guides for those reports' explicit completeness and permission rules, rather than treating every operational report as an equivalent source of population metrics.

pages.title: 5.6 Survival Percentage
pages.html:
Use Survival Percentage to review recorded deaths relative to animal exposure over a period. The card defaults to the current month through today and your default Company. It includes only permitted batches marked Is Livestock Item, with Items counted in Nos or Unit. Optional Company, Item, Batch, house, and date filters narrow the scope.

Period survival is 100 × (opening population + animals entering the scope − deaths) / (opening population + animals entering the scope). It combines animal counts rather than averaging batch percentages. Sales and explicitly separate Culling-type issues are departures, not deaths. All issues posted under the Mortality type count as deaths; culling recorded under that same type cannot be distinguished automatically. Internal transfers and valuation-only Repacks net out across the selected scope. Transfers into a selected house count as entrants to that house. The card shows Unavailable for a missing denominator, stock corrections, incomplete batch transformations, unreadable/unclassified stock issues, or invalid negative balances. Its percentage is an operational period rate, not a lifetime cohort survival estimate. Automatic percentage-change statistics are disabled because they are a different metric.

For a stable opening population of 10,000 and 652 classified deaths, survival is 93.48%. Review source classifications before interpreting a difference from closing/opening population.

pages.title: 5.7 Number Cards
pages.html:
Number Cards

Use Number Cards to check your flock summaries at a glance. They normally use your default Company and the current month through today. Optional Company, Item, Batch, House, and date filters narrow their scope where configured. Dashboard eligibility uses livestock-marked Batches; verify the field before troubleshooting a zero.

Survival Percentage

Shows the operational period survival percentage, combining animal counts rather than averaging Batch percentages. It excludes separately classified culling from deaths. Read the dedicated survival guide for denominator and unavailable cases.

Feed Consumed

Sums stock quantities from submitted Feeding / Material Issue entries linked to eligible livestock Batches, converted to Kg. It does not count draft entries or purchases sitting in the feed store. A zero means no matching recorded consumption; an unavailable value can indicate invalid units, inaccessible details, or missing house allocation.

Read this value as kilograms of feed, not currency.

Feed Consumed card with a verified kg value.

Internal Feed Conversion Ratio

Feed Conversion Ratio is kg feed divided by kg live-weight gain between valid measurements. It is a ratio, not a percentage or currency. The shared interval rules are also used by the batch performance report.

For every active Batch/House in scope, the calculation uses the latest two measurements within the selected period. Those measurements must have different timestamps, explicit Company/House/Kg UOM, valid samples and positive average weights. The interval needs positive population, positive biomass gain, and no unsupported population-changing movements. Relevant feed must be posted in the interval. Several eligible house/batch intervals are aggregated as total feed divided by total biomass gain, not an average of ratios.

Example: 100 animals growing from 1.0 to 1.2 kg with 40 kg feed give FCR 2. One Weight Record cannot establish that gain. Missing or invalid intervals return unavailable/N/A with a reason; do not create an invented opening weight to obtain a number.

Internal FCR showing 2 for the documented stable-population example.

pages.title: 5.8 Dashboard Charts
pages.html:
Use Daily Population and Mortality Trend to follow changes in your animal counts. Keep the interval set to Daily for both charts. Their values are counts, even if the chart setup form also contains a Currency field.

Daily Population

  • Chart Type: Custom; source: Daily Population; display: Line; Time Series enabled.
  • Each point is historical daily closing animal population, including quiet days carried forward from earlier movements.
  • Opening history before the displayed range is needed to establish the first day's closing balance.
  • Default scope uses the user's default Company and accessible livestock-marked Batches; optional Item, Batch, and House filters narrow it.

Daily Population line showing a quiet day and a subsequent verified increase.

Mortality Trend

  • Chart Type: Custom; source: Mortality Trend Source; display: Line; Time Series enabled.
  • Each point shows classified posted mortality quantities, not the number of Stock Entry documents and not a mortality percentage.
  • Source access, stock allocations, and classification determine what is included.

Mortality Trend showing the same known loss day with an animal-count axis.

pages.title: 5.9 Performance Alerts
pages.html:
Set up performance alerts to notify the person responsible when your flock needs attention. Your enabled rules run daily and create assigned ToDos with the evidence needed for follow-up. New follow-ups use a standard System Notification.

Set up rules

  1. Open Performance Alert Rules from the Livestock workspace/sidebar or search for Livestock Performance Alert Rule. Stock Managers and System Managers can manage rules.
  2. Select Company, alert type, and an enabled System User responsible for follow-up. Optionally restrict the rule to a Livestock Item and non-group House/Warehouse in that Company.
  3. Enter the thresholds for that alert type. Thresholds have no biological defaults: choose them
  4. Mark applicable Batches Is Livestock Item. Their Items must be batch-tracked stock Items counted in Nos or Unit.
  5. Give the responsible user read access to Company, Item, Batch, House, and all source documents used by the rule. A filtered subset of ledger entries or measurements is not accepted as complete evidence.
  6. Enable the rule. Enabled rules of the same alert type and Company cannot overlap Item/House scope. For example, an unrestricted Company mortality rule cannot coexist with a mortality rule for one Item within that Company. Different alert types may cover the same flock.

The scheduler must be enabled and workers running on the site. Checks use your site's configured timezone. Ask your administrator to verify scheduled processing and the responsible user's source-record access. It sends no reminders until rules have been configured and enabled.

Scoped alert rule with responsible user, explicit thresholds, and Enabled setting.

Detection rules

Alert type Trigger and evidence
Mortality On the last completed farm day, both minimum death count and mortality percentage thresholds are reached. Percentage is deaths ÷ (opening population + incoming animals) × 100, using the survival calculation's stock-validity checks.
Below-target Weight The latest valid average kg/animal measurement falls below its measurement-age profile target by at least the configured shortfall percentage. Requires a submitted performance profile, Hatch/Birth Date, positive target, valid sample size, and known house.
Overdue Weighing Today is later than the last valid weighing date plus Maximum Weighing Gap. If never weighed during the current occupancy period, use the date stock first became positive in the house.
Overdue Treatment A saved Veterinary Diagnosis remains Pending and its end date is before today. This is an overdue treatment follow-up, not proof that an individual dose was missed.

Population and weight alerts are evaluated separately for each Company/Batch/House. Your stock quantities are read from historical ledger allocations, including supported batch fields and Serial and Batch Bundles without duplicate counting. Mortality is measured for yesterday, even if the job is run again during today. Only issues classified as Mortality count as deaths; separately classified culling does not.

Stock corrections, unclassified animal issues, and unresolved batch transformations can make the mortality denominator unavailable. An invalid denominator is Unknown, not a zero death rate. A completed day with no livestock exposure has no current mortality condition.

Weights need explicit Company, historical house, Kg UOM, positive average weight, and a positive whole sample size within the population at measurement time. Older weights before the latest zero-to-positive occupancy change do not satisfy the current weighing requirement. Valuation-only Repacks are netted by voucher and do not reset the arrival date. A below-target weight can remain an active condition until a newer valid measurement or revised verified target supports recovery; the evidence date is displayed. Missing measurements are handled by the weighing-gap rule rather than invented growth values.

Pending diagnoses are drafts in the existing workflow: submission requires Completed status. The treatment check therefore includes saved Pending drafts. It uses the diagnosis end date, not individual treatment-plan doses. Company/Batch-wide rules can follow a diagnosis without a recorded house; House-scoped rules need its explicit capitalisation warehouse or its correctly linked medicine issue's explicit house. The current Batch location is not used to guess a past location.

Follow-up and recovery

Each new issue creates a High-priority ToDo, assigned to the responsible user and due on detection day. Stock/weight follow-ups reference Batch; treatment follow-ups reference Veterinary Diagnosis. The initial description contains the evidence and a source link.

Generated High-priority ToDo with evidence date, condition, assignment, and source link.

Use the ToDo's Latest Alert Evidence, Evidence Date, Condition State, and Last Evaluated On fields to inspect current detection results. Repeated evaluations update these fields without replacing user-written descriptions or creating duplicate tasks. Use standard comments and ToDo status for follow-up.

Condition state Meaning
Active The latest valid evaluation breaches the configured rule.
Cleared Valid evidence establishes recovery, no current stock exposure/occupancy, or completed/cancelled treatment follow-up.
Unknown Evidence is missing, invalid, inaccessible, or no longer matches the rule scope. It does not establish recovery.

There is at most one open system-managed follow-up per condition scope. Closing or cancelling a ToDo acknowledges the current episode: it stays closed/cancelled while that condition persists. An acknowledged episode must first clear before a later breach creates another ToDo.

Acknowledged ToDo with status and retained managed evidence.

On Company, configure Auto-close Performance ToDos on Recovery:

  • Off (default): mark the condition Cleared but leave an open ToDo for manual closure. If it recurs while that ToDo remains open, reuse the open follow-up.
  • On: close an open performance ToDo after confirmed recovery. Later recurrence creates a new ToDo. Existing acknowledged Closed/Cancelled tasks are not reopened.

Unknown evaluations preserve previous evidence and never close tasks. Disabled rules pause monitoring; they do not establish recovery. Scopes that disappear from eligible inputs are marked Unknown rather than silently resolved. Standard Error Logs record rule failures and unavailable inputs for administrator review; one failed rule does not stop others.

Alert identity and evaluation fields are maintained by the detector and protected server-side. Change the rule to change responsible ownership. Managed ToDos cannot be deleted through the normal form/API because their history prevents duplicate episodes; close or cancel them instead. Unrelated ToDos are unaffected.

Notifications

The app installs Livestock Performance Follow-up, a standard Frappe Notification configuration:

  • Document: ToDo; event: New; channel: System Notification; type: Alert.
  • Condition: a system-managed performance scope with Active condition.
  • Recipient: the email identity of the ToDo's allocated user, stored in a protected field so special user IDs such as Administrator can also be resolved.

New ToDos notify once; routine updates, acknowledgement, and recovery send no additional alert messages. Notifications respect standard user notification settings. A recurrence that creates a new ToDo sends a new notification; reusing an already-open task does not.

pages.title: 6.1 Calculations and Definitions
pages.html:
Use these definitions to reconcile your report values with your stock movements, measurements, and targets. Keep Company, House, and dates consistent when comparing results.

Population and survival

Daily closing population is the historical batch stock balance at day end in the selected Company/House scope. Transfers have source and destination movements; a same-batch valuation Repack does not create new animals.

Period survival is:

exposure = opening animals + animals entering the scope
survival % = 100 × (exposure − classified deaths) / exposure

Sales and separately classified culling are departures rather than deaths. House entrants include animals transferred into that house. Invalid stock corrections or incomplete transformations can make the denominator unavailable. This is a period operational measure, not lifetime cohort survival.

Biological age and targets

age day = measurement/report day − verified Hatch/Birth Date
feed target kg = sum(daily closing animals × exact-age intake g / 1,000)
hen-day yield % = 100 × configured eggs / sum(daily closing hens)
yield target % = sum(daily closing hens × daily yield target %) / sum(daily closing hens)

Age zero is the Hatch/Birth Date. Target lookup is exact, with no interpolation. Feed/yield targets need a target for every day with positive population. Invalid negative balances or missing exposure do not produce partial targets. Hen-day yield requires an all-female laying profile.

Weight, FCR, and variance

biomass gain kg = eligible population × (ending average kg − opening average kg)
interval FCR = interval feed kg / positive biomass gain kg
variance = actual − target
variance % = 100 × (actual − target) / target

The simple interval formula requires a valid stable population and supported measured interval. Weight targets use measurement age; FCR targets use ending measurement age. Several eligible intervals aggregate feed and biomass rather than averaging FCRs. Percentage variance is unavailable for zero targets. Egg-yield variance is actual minus target in percentage points.

Blank targets mean unspecified; explicit zero targets remain valid. Missing data is unavailable, not zero. Lower feed can indicate underfeeding, so variance signs do not automatically establish good or bad performance.

See Target Comparisons for full eligibility details.

pages.title: 6.2 Document Statuses and Cancellations
pages.html:
Check both the document's submission state and its activity Status before deciding whether it is ready for reporting. Some records, such as Weight Record, are saved without a Submit step; others need submission or a Completed status.

Document Included state / effect
Stock transaction Submitted, non-cancelled postings establish inventory; drafts do not
Weight Record Saved, non-cancelled, valid measurements can be used without submission
Livestock Event Completed activities appear in lifecycle history; Daily Farm Entry initially saves Open
Veterinary Diagnosis Submitted Completed records support completed treatment history; saved Pending drafts support overdue follow-up
Performance Profile Submitted profile required for assigned target comparisons
Performance ToDo Open/Closed/Cancelled represents follow-up status; Active/Cleared/Unknown is separately managed evidence

Correcting records

  1. Open the source document and inspect its linked records.
  2. Use authorized standard edits for editable saved records.
  3. For submitted transactions, follow ERPNext cancellation/amendment rules and posting restrictions.
  4. Recheck stock/valuation, report dates, and dependent records after correction.

Cancelling Veterinary Diagnosis cancels its linked Capitalization Repack before its Medical issue, subject to ERPNext checks. This behavior must not be assumed for every other source document. Review dependent entries explicitly.

Submitted profiles use cancellation/amendment to preserve versions. Reassigning a Batch to another submitted profile changes historical comparisons. Managed performance ToDos cannot be deleted normally because their history prevents duplicate alert episodes; close or cancel them instead.

pages.title: Overview
pages.html:
Kenya Compliance via Slade 360 Advantage is an integration application that connects ERPNext with the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) eTIMS platform through Slade360 Advantage, an approved compliance middleware provider, supporting both the Virtual Sales Control Unit (VSCU) and Online Sales Control Unit (OSCU) frameworks.

The application enables businesses to automatically transmit transactional data such as sales invoices, purchase records, inventory information, and customer data from ERPNext to KRA in compliance with Kenyan tax regulations. It embeds compliance directly into everyday business workflows, removing the need for manual reporting.

Why This Integration Matters

The Electronic Tax Invoice Management System (eTIMS) is a mandatory system introduced by KRA requiring businesses to generate compliant invoices and submit transaction data to the tax authority.

Without automation, this process can be time-consuming, error-prone, and difficult to maintain consistently.

By integrating ERPNext with eTIMS via Slade 360 Advantage, businesses benefit from:

  • Regulatory compliance with KRA requirements
  • Support for both VSCU and OSCU compliance models
  • Automated transmission of transaction data
  • Improved accuracy in tax reporting
  • Reduced manual intervention
  • Better audit readiness and traceability

How It Works (High-Level)

The integration operates seamlessly within ERPNext workflows.

When a transaction such as a Sales Invoice is created, the system prepares a compliant data payload based on KRA requirements. This data is securely sent to Slade360 Advantage through an API. Slade360 Advantage processes the request and forwards it to the eTIMS platform using the appropriate compliance framework.

Once processed, a response is returned and stored in ERPNext. The transaction is then updated with compliance status and any reference details from KRA.

This entire process happens in the background with minimal user intervention.

Key Capabilities

The application provides a full compliance layer within ERPNext, covering:

  • Sales Invoice Submission: Automatic transmission of sales transactions to eTIMS as part of normal invoicing workflows.
  • Item and Customer Registration: Synchronization of product, customer, and inventory data with eTIMS requirements.
  • Compliance Tracking: Visibility into submission status, responses, and errors directly within ERPNext.
  • Error Handling and Retry: Mechanisms to handle failed submissions and allow for retries without data loss.

Role of Slade360 Advantage

Slade360 Advantage acts as an intermediary layer between ERPNext and KRA eTIMS.

It is responsible for handling secure communication with KRA systems, validating and transforming data payloads, supporting both VSCU and OSCU integrations, and ensuring adherence to KRA API standards.

Access to eTIMS through Slade 360 Advantage requires prior onboarding and approval.

pages.title: How It Works

headings.title: Step 4: Processing by Slade360 Advantage and eTIMS

pages.html:
Kenya Compliance via Slade360 Advantage integrates ERPNext with the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) eTIMS platform through Slade360 Advantage, allowing tax-related transactions to be processed and transmitted automatically as part of normal ERP workflows.

The integration supports both Virtual Sales Control Unit (VSCU) and Online Sales Control Unit (OSCU) compliance models and is designed to operate in the background with minimal user intervention while ensuring transactions remain compliant with KRA requirements.

High-Level Flow

The integration follows a structured transaction flow between ERPNext, Slade360 Advantage, and KRA eTIMS.

Step 1: Transaction Creation in ERPNext

A user creates or submits a transaction in ERPNext, such as:

  • Sales Invoice
  • Credit Note
  • Item Registration
  • Customer Registration

The application validates the transaction and checks whether it qualifies for eTIMS submission.

Step 2: Payload Preparation

Once the transaction is validated, the integration prepares a structured payload formatted according to Slade360 Advantage and KRA eTIMS requirements.

Step 3: Secure API Communication

The prepared payload is securely transmitted from ERPNext to Slade360 Advantage using authenticated API requests.

Slade360 Advantage acts as the compliance middleware responsible for securely communicating with KRA systems.

Step 4: Processing by Slade360 Advantage and eTIMS

Slade360 Advantage validates the incoming payload and forwards the request to KRA eTIMS through the configured VSCU or OSCU channel.

During this stage:

  • Data validation checks are performed
  • Tax compliance rules are enforced
  • KRA reference information may be generated

Step 5: Response Handling

After processing, a response is returned through Slade360 Advantage back to ERPNext.

The response may include:

  • Submission status
  • Reference numbers
  • QR URL or compliance identifiers
  • Validation messages
  • Error details (if any)

The response is stored within ERPNext for audit and tracking purposes.

Step 6: ERPNext Transaction Update
